ACR0232.methodology: ARB Compliance Offset Protocol: Capturing and Destroying Methane from Manure Management Systems
ACR0232.description: The Dry Creek Dairy Biofactor Project is a dairy digester system that was built to capture the biogas from dairy manure, the majority of which would have been stored in an open lagoon system prior to project implementation. The biogas that is captured from the digester system is used to generate electricity through three generator sets. Any excess biogas not combusted by the gen-sets is combusted in an open flare. Biogas produced by the digester is monitored continuously using thermal mass flowmeters.

ACR0242.methodology: ARB Compliance Offset Protocol: Mine Methane Capture Projects
ACR0242.description: The project consists of the collection and combustion of mine methane from the abandoned Cambria Slope No 33 mine in Cambria County, PA. The Project is in the Township of Ebensburg, PA. The primary methane source is a surface well located south of Ebensburg, which was drilled after the mine was abandoned. The mine methane is destroyed by an enclosed flare. A new methane source was added to the project during 2023 (RP6): post-mining gob wells drilled into the mine during active mining operations. The mine gas is destroyed by a microflare (enclosed flare). This was an early action project registered with Verra's VCS Program. It removed mine methane from the same surface well and piped the raw gas to a gas processing plant. The plant upgraded the gas which was compressed and injected into a natural gas distribution pipeline. Raw mine methane was also combusted by an engine to produce power required by the gas production plant. These destruction devices are no longer part of the Project.

ACR0243.methodology: ARB Compliance Offset Protocol: Mine Methane Capture Projects
ACR0243.description: Installation of a facility to collect and utilize CMM from a temporarily idle coal mine. CMM is withdrawn using vacuum pumps from bore holes and then destroyed either via an enclosed flare or three electricity generators. Flow of CMM is measured continuously using flow meters for each destruction device. Methane concentration is measured continuously using gas analyzers. All data is recorded by a data logger.

ACR0261.methodology: AM0065 Replacement of SF6 with alternate cover gas in the magnesium industry
ACR0261.siteLocation: 60 miles west of Salt Lake City, UT
ACR0261.description: SF6 has been widely used in the magnesium industry for more than 30 years.  SF6 is a highly-stable molecule – a major reason why it is such a concern for global warming as it can stay in the atmosphere absorbing solar radiation for 3,200 years.  Because of its stability and non-toxicity, the gas is used by magnesium die casters, producers and recyclers to protect the molten metal from reacting with air.  Without this protection, molten magnesium will oxidize and form magnesium oxide (MgO) deposits that greatly reduce the quality and strength of the final product.  The effective cover gas stabilizes the MgO surface film to form a protective layer that prevents further oxidation. For years, the industry has tried to find alternatives to SF6, which generally gets emitted in the process. US Magnesium has undertaken an effort to convert from SF6 to HFC-134a, itself a greenhouse gas but with a much lower global warming potential.

ACR0380.methodology: ACR Methodology for Quantifying Nitrous Oxide (N2O) Emissions Reductions from Reduced Use of Nitrogen Fertilizer on Agricultural Crops
ACR0380.description: The Project quantifies emission reductions (in the form of nitrous oxide or N2O) arising from a reduction in the rate of fertilizer (synthetic and/or organic) applied to corn crops on farms of the North Central Region (NCR). The rate reduction arises as a result of the adoption of fertilizer Best Management Practices (BMPs) aimed at application of the right fertilizer type at the right time, using the right placement and at the right rate in order to minimize denitrification, leaching and run-off, and volatilization, and thereby increasing fertilizer efficiency. Moves towards efficient fertilizer use are happening on a global scale, with increased recognition of the dual needs of providing sufficient food for a rapidly increasing population with limited resources, and addressing climate change issues, where fertilizer application is perceived as a significant emission source.

ACR0390.methodology: ARB Compliance Offset Protocol: Capturing and Destroying Methane from Manure Management Systems
ACR0390.description: The Clean Fuel Partners Dane County Biodigester utilizes manure from three animal facilities: Ripp's Dairy Valley and Enders Dairy in Dane, Wisconsin; and White Gold Dairy in Waunakee, Wisconsin. The biogas control and combustion system first generated biogas in March 2011. The Project consists of three, 1.25 million-gallon capacity, above ground, complete mix digesters with dual membrane covers. Biogas from the digester is primarily destroyed in two GE Jenbacher engines, each rated at 1.03 MW. The Project also has a backup flare to burn any excess gas.

ACR0392.methodology: ARB Compliance Offset Protocol: Capturing and Destroying Methane from Manure Management Systems
ACR0392.description: The Majestic Meadows Facility digester utilizes manure from Majestic Crossing Dairy in Sheboygan Falls, Wisconsin. The Project consists of one rectangular, in-ground digester, designed by Digested Organics LLC. This system is Digester Organics' first fully Integrated Manure Management System (IMMS™) that processes 20,000 gallons of manure per day, effectively harvesting energy through biogas generation, concentrating nutrients for more targeted crop use, and reclaiming clean water for farm use and surface water discharge. The system is a modular, scalable, and tunable high-rate anaerobic digester that converts over 90% of the organic matter into biogas with retention times of only 5 days. The digester system has a 100,000-gallon capacity and is operated at mesophilic temperatures. Biogas from the digester is primarily destroyed in a boiler which produces heat to maintain digester temperatures and a backup flare to burn any excess gas.

The project is managed for carbon sequestration, provision of wildlife habitat, protection of local water quality, and recreation. The forest consists primarily of mixed hardwoods including various oak species, American beech, yellow poplar, maples, American sycamore, and hickory, as well as scattered stands of pine and hemlock.

ACR0587.methodology: ACR Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Non-Federal U.S. Forestlands
ACR0587.description: The Anew - North Maine Woods Forestry Project is located on 86,221 acres of Northern Hardwood and Northern Conifer forest in Maine's North Woods, an area of more than 10 million acres of timberland, the majority of which is privately owned. The project area has a long history of commercial timber harvesting and the landowner, Tree-Star Timberland, acquired this property as a timberland investment, with the objective of obtaining competitive returns through commercial forest management. Revenues from a carbon project will allow for harvest levels to be reduced meaningfully below the thresholds allowed by the property's current Forest Management Plan, as carbon payments supplant income that would otherwise be achieved through more intensive commercial timbering. The forest management activities under the carbon project will also foster habitat for rare and threatened species in the area including the Canada Lynx and American Marten.

ACR0588.methodology: ACR Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Non-Federal U.S. Forestlands
ACR0588.description: The Anew - Big Six Forestry Project is located on 22,067 acres in the industrial forests of northern Maine. It is owned by Big Six Land and Timber Inc., a for profit company with the intent of generating revenue through a blend of sustainable timber harvesting and maple syrup operations. In recent years, servicing the debt on the property's mortgage has proven increasingly challenging and the landowners have been forced to consider abandoning the maple syrup operation and adopting a considerably more aggressive commercial harvest strategy across the property in order to generate the requisite revenue. The proceeds associated with the implementation of the carbon project have allowed the owners to avoid the need for near term harvests, other than maple stand improvement thinnings to improve the sugaring operation, and to pursue a management strategy involving zero commercial harvesting for the next several decades.

ACR0590.methodology: ACR Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Non-Federal U.S. Forestlands
ACR0590.description: Home to several endangered species, the Anew - Blue Ridge Escarpment Forestry Project protects 5,795 acres of southern hardwood and pine forests in the Blue Ridge mountains of upstate South Carolina. The property is owned by Naturaland Trust, an organization dedicated to protecting the Blue Ridge Region from further development. The properties within their portfolio have historically been managed for a variety of resources, including timber products, and are not subject to any legally binding easements or harvesting constraints. If faced with financial challenges, harvesting would be a lucrative revenue generator to support Naturaland Trust's needs. By providing a continuous source of income for the Trust, the carbon project will provide valuable financial support for the organization, relieving pressures to harvest and ensuring the protection and enhancement of forest stocks on the subject properties for decades to come.

Forests in the project region have been subject to mining and timbering, which still occur on Doyon lands today. The project supports Doyon's mission to be a leading innovator amongst Alaska's Native Corporations and to promote the economic and social well-being of Alaska Natives. Carbon funding will contribute to job opportunities and regional economic growth within the community, investment in sustainability infrastructure (e.g. clean water distribution stations, LEED building construction, restoration of riparian zones), and targeted forest management for cultural use and recreation. The financial success of the carbon project will reduce economic pressures for expansion of mining across Doyon's broader land base.

Located on over 100,000 acres in Michigan's Pigeon River Country State Forest, the project will provide significant climate benefits through carbon sequestration via sustainable forest management. The project area is the life-blood of the region, serving as the epicenter of Michigan's elk range and providing clean and cold water to support trout in the Sturgeon, Pigeon, and Black rivers and their tributaries. The landowner, Baskahegan Company, owns over 150,000 acres of forestland in Maine including another carbon project directly adjacent to Tomah Highlands, and has been operating in the forestry industry for over 100 years. Baskahegan Co. has been a leader in sustainable forest management in the region for decades, implementing low impact harvesting methods and longer harvesting rotations. However, given the current economics of industrial forestry in Maine, this strategy has led to diminishing returns and has forced Baskahegan Co. to harvest greater volumes of timber than they would like over recent years. Carbon projects and the associated revenues have offered an alternative path for them to meet their mission of long-term, sustainable forestry without increasing harvests on their forestlands.

ACR0633.description: The Anew - White Mountain Forestry Project is located on 11,341 acres of Northern Appalachia hardwood and conifer forest in New Hampshire's White Mountains. The land is owned by Chocorua Forestlands, LLC, a privately held company that owns a large sawmill and manages their forestlands for multiple uses, such as commercial wood products, firewood and maple syrup production, and local recreation. Historically, when faced with increased financial pressures or heightened demand for firewood, Chocorua Forestlands was pressed to ramp-up harvesting to fulfill the supply for their mill and generate necessary income. Carbon revenues make it possible for the landowner to achieve their goal of improving forest stocking, structure, and species composition, while not having to rely on harvesting proceeds as a sole source of revenue to achieve this goal. Participation in this carbon project ensures sustainable management of the timberland and associated climate benefits over the next four decades.

ACR0639.description: The Northeast Kingdom Forestry Project is located on 10,210 acres of Northern Hardwood forests in northern Vermont and New Hampshire. The land has been under private family ownership for multiple generations with a history of commercial forest management, but current financial challenges and the fragmented nature of the property threaten the family's ability to maintain the property's considerable forest carbon stocking. In the absence of the carbon project commitment, forest stocks could be dramatically reduced on the property due to increasing financial pressure to clear forestland for agricultural applications, residential development, and large scale solar and wind projects. With sustainable timber management underpinning the carbon project and a maple sugaring operation, the project area supplies jobs for community members, supports the local and regional economies, and provides an island of habitat for a wide variety of animal species in an otherwise fragmented forest landscape.

ACR0643.description: The project encompasses 159,656 acres, representing Bayfield County's Forest holdings as the 3rd largest expanse of county forest in Wisconsin. The county has practiced commercial harvesting across its ownership since the establishment of the county forest system in 1927, and revenues from timbering have represented the largest single source of income for the county. However, because Bayfield County now stands to recognize a significant new source of revenue from the establishment of a carbon project, County managers are reducing harvests meaningfully below annual harvest allocation limits and actively considering further curtailment of harvesting to prioritize greater carbon sequestration. The Bayfield carbon project is the first forest carbon project initiated on county lands in the country, and the bold and progressive action of Bayfield's forest management team has already inspired other counties to enroll in similar projects.

ACR0663.methodology: ACR Certified Reclaimed HFC Refrigerants, Propellants, and Fire Suppressants
ACR0663.description: Fielding Environmental ("Fielding") is one of only two major refrigerant reclamation and recycling companies in Canada. Refrigerant reclamation and recycling is a core business unit for Fielding and it includes ODS and non-ODS refrigerants that come from various sectors across the country including the automotive sector and the refrigeration and air conditioning sector. Fielding receives refrigerants from authorized wholesalers or directly from contractors and end-users that have collected refrigerant from end-of-life equipment or after equipment retrofits. Through an innovative and customized process Fielding reclaims refrigerants, which are then sold back into the refrigerant market, avoiding the use of an equivalent volume of virgin refrigerants, and their eventual GHG emissions.

ACR0664.methodology: ACR Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Non-Federal U.S. Forestlands
ACR0664.description: The Anew - Connecticut River Forestry Project is located on 22,735 acres of northern hardwood and northeast conifer forest, encompassing several river corridors and reservoirs across New England. The land is owned by Great River Hydro, LLC, a privately held, for profit corporation that derives revenue from hydroelectric power generation and commercial timber management. Within the last decade, Great River Hydro has tapped into commercial harvesting as an added revenue stream to offset increasing land management and ownership costs. Under the carbon project, Great River Hydro's management priorities have shifted from maximizing their harvesting potential to maximizing carbon sequestration across their land base—a strategy that more closely aligns with the company's core values as one of New England's largest generators of renewable energy. Resulting carbon funds will be allocated to ownership objectives, such as improving wildlife habitat and upgrading existing recreational facilities.

ACR0673.methodology: ACR Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Non-Federal U.S. Forestlands
ACR0673.description: The Anew – Two-Hearted Forestry Project is located on approximately 23,294 acres of northern hardwood forest and conifer bog, distributed throughout Luce and Marquette Counties in the Upper Peninsula of Michigan, and owned by The Nature Conservancy (TNC). Although owned by TNC, this property has been managed for commercial timber as it is not subject to any legally binding easements or harvesting constraints. However, the anticipated financial returns from this project have significantly changed the management outlook of the property, leading TNC to pivot to a harvest regime considerably less aggressive than was originally outlined in their Forest Management Plan (FMP). The carbon credits generated from the project will reflect TNC's commitment to increasing forest stocks under the carbon project management regime above those stocks that would have been maintained on the property under the preexisting FMP.

ACR0684.description: The Anew – Rusk County Forestry Project is located on approximately 79,300 acres of northern hardwood, aspen, and oak forest in Rusk County, Wisconsin. The County has practiced intensive commercial harvesting across its ownership since first enrolling its land under Wisconsin's Forest Crop Law in 1931 and revenues from timbering currently represent the largest source of annual income for the County, outside of tax collections. In recent decades, the County has experienced budget challenges as result of tax levies being capped, despite rising maintenance and administrative costs. Typically, increasing commercial harvesting is one of the primary means to filling the budget funding gap. However, with the establishment of the carbon project, credit sales associated with standing trees provide a viable alternative revenue source and should allow the County to meet budget needs without placing greater pressure on its forests.

The project area has a long history of commercial harvesting, and the geographic region is a major hub for the wood products industry. Revenues from a carbon project will incentivize the reduction of harvest levels meaningfully below what is detailed in the property's existing 10-year management plan. KFM's parent company, Acadian Timber Corp, is using this carbon project as a test case for the viability of supplanting timber harvest revenues with income from carbon credit sales, and upon profitable returns, will consider this strategy across their broader land base.

The IFM carbon project supports Windrock in maintaining timber harvest levels below the growth rate to encourage the health and value of the forest, while increasing carbon stored.  Project objectives also include sustainable forest management for long-term income, and restoration forestry.

ACR0702.methodology: ACR Destruction of Ozone Depleting Substances from International Sources
ACR0702.description: The purpose of the project is to avoid the release of refrigerant emissions such as CFCs and HCFCs to the atmosphere that have high global warming potential (GWP) values. Refrigerant Management Canada (RMC) administers a voluntary refrigerant ODS destruction program. As there are currently no regulations to collect and destroy ODS at the end of a product's useful life, they can be reused or stockpiled indefinitely resulting in their gradual release to the atmosphere. Through RMC's voluntary program, surplus ODS from Canadian refrigeration and air conditioning industries are transferred to a destruction facility where ODS is destroyed through incineration.

ACR0732.methodology: ACR Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Non-Federal U.S. Forestlands
ACR0732.description: This project is in Northern California's Mid-Klamath basin comprising 12,364 acres of diverse conifer forest assemblage, with globally significant biodiversity, important headwaters and endangered species, alpine meadows, and wilderness trailheads linking to the Pacific Crest Trail. The purpose of this IFM project is to increase the forest carbon stocks during the project period by implementing management actions that go above and beyond common practices by creating expanded voluntary buffers, special wildlife areas, reduced intensity silvicultural practices, and increased rotation ages via FSC-certified management practices. The result of these changed management practices will be increased carbon storage on the landscape. Also, this management regime will improve the overall forest health and resiliency of the project area, while creating and maintaining habitat for a range of wildlife species. Carbon revenue will replace some forgone timber revenue over the project period

ACR0734.methodology: ACR Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Non-Federal U.S. Forestlands
ACR0734.description: This project is located between Etna and Fort Jones in Scott Valley, California. The project area contains 7,798 acres of diverse conifer forest assemblage, with globally significant biodiversity, important headwaters, alpine meadows, and wilderness trailheads linking to the Pacific Crest Trail. The Sugar Creek drainage, part of the Wildcat project area, is home to "the Miracle Mile" – one of the richest conifer assemblages on Earth. The purpose of this IFM project is to increase the forest carbon stocks by implementing management actions that go above and beyond common practices by creating voluntary buffers, special wildlife areas, reduced intensity silvicultural practices, and increased rotation ages via FSC-certified management. The result of these changed management practices will be more carbon stored on the landscape while improving forest health and resilience, and creating habitat for wildlife. Carbon revenue will replace some forgone timber harvest revenue during the period.
ACR0734.berkeleyNotes: The project developer in v9 was Ecotrust Forest Management, Inc.

ACR0735.methodology: ACR Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Non-Federal U.S. Forestlands
ACR0735.siteLocation: Oxford and Cumberland Counties, Maine and Coos County, New Hampshire
ACR0735.description: The project is a joint effort between Loon Echo Land Trust and Mahoosuc Land Trust to combine forestland in a PDA project to facilitate entry into the carbon market, and increase land conservation paired with carbon sequestration. These two 501(c)(3) non-profit organizations have similar conservation missions, work in the same region of Maine, and are accredited by the Land Trust Accreditation Commission. The project is the first to arise from the Carbon Offset Pilot Program, a partnership between Finite Carbon and Land Trust Alliance. The project area is dominated by a mix of hardwood (maple/beech/birch) and softwood (spruce/pine/fir) forest types typical of Maine forests. The land trusts manage the land as model forests, focused on public access, general health, habitat, species, age-class and structural diversity and quality timber production over long rotations, along with revenue generation to facilitate land conservation and stewardship.

ACR0754.methodology: ACR Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Non-Federal U.S. Forestlands
ACR0754.description: Allagash Headwaters is located on about 14,815 acres in the industrial forests of northern Maine and owned by Hull Forestlands Maine. The Hull family of companies, which includes timberland scattered across New England and a sawmill in Pomfret Center Connecticut, focuses on the production of traditional forest products. Throughout the project's geographic region, industrial forestland like the Allagash property is often heavily harvested through clear-cutting and high-grading, in the service of maximizing the NPV of the forest asset. The previous landowner cut more than 70% of the 20-year sustainable harvest levels in the 5 years prior to Hull ownership. Carbon revenues allow Hull to harvest more sustainably, leading to fewer disturbances on the landscape, increased diversity of forest makeup and health, accelerated carbon storage, and improved habitat protection for species of concern, such as the Canada Lynx (threatened) and the Rusty Blackbird (species of special concern in Maine).

ACR0772.methodology: ACR Destruction of Ozone Depleting Substances and High-GWP Foam
ACR0772.description: The purpose of the project is to avoid the release of refrigerant emissions such as CFCs and HCFCs to the atmosphere that have high global warming potential (GWP) values. Refrigerant Management Canada (RMC) administers a voluntary refrigerant ODS destruction program. As there are currently no regulations to collect and destroy ODS at the end of a product's useful life, they can be reused or stockpiled indefinitely resulting in their gradual release to the atmosphere. Through RMC's voluntary program, surplus ODS from Canadian refrigeration and air conditioning industries are transferred to a destruction facility where ODS is destroyed through incineration.

ACR0785.methodology: ACR Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Non-Federal U.S. Forestlands
ACR0785.siteLocation: Somerset, Penobscot, Oxford, Waldo, Kennebec, and Lincoln Counties, Maine
ACR0785.description: Through this project, Bessey Development is protecting 20,000+ acres of Maine forests under the American Carbon Registry's Improved Forest Management protocol. With lands near Augusta, Maine, the state capital, the project conserves native forest at risk of conversion through 2062, while maintaining and accruing additional sequestered carbon. The multi-generational family owner practices sustainable forest management, carbon sequestration and land conservation to benefit rural community economic development, wildlife populations, recreation, air quality and water quality. The mature and diverse forest is American Tree Farm System certified, meeting the highest standards for sustainability, and consists of an even mixture of softwood and hardwood species. Bessey allows unrestricted public access for recreation on their woodlands, as is traditional in New England.

ACR0786.methodology: ACR Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Non-Federal U.S. Forestlands

Through 2062, the project conserves carbon-rich forests at high risk of conversion, while maintaining and accruing additional sequestered carbon in biodiverse hardwood forests adjacent to the Savannah River. Scott Woodlands is SFI-certified and dedicated to leadership and sustainability in all aspects of forestland stewardship and the wood products industry. Its commitment to sustainable forest management, carbon sequestration, and land conservation brings benefits to rural community economic development, wildlife populations, and air and water quality. The Scott forestlands consist of approximately half pine stands and half well-stocked, mixed hardwood stands, adjacent to and near the Savannah River. This intact forest helps protect and maintain the Savannah River, which provides drinking water to 1.4 million people, including two of Georgia's major metro areas, Augusta and Savannah.

ACR0790.methodology: ACR Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Non-Federal U.S. Forestlands

These carbon-rich forests are located in areas with a high risk of conversion, maintaining and sequestering additional carbon in a highly biodiverse region that provides climate resilient habitat for threatened and endangered species. Rooted in bioregionalism, ACE is a non-profit, community first partnership of dedicated landowners and businesses in Appalachia. The land in the ACE IFM project consists of intact mixed hardwood forest that provides habitat connectivity through essential wildlife corridors and climate resilience with its unique topography, both above and belowground. It also helps protect regional water quality and provides access to iconic and beloved outdoor recreation areas. ACR0851.methodology: ACR Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Non-Federal U.S. Forestlands
ACR0851.description: The Anew – Big Poplar Forestry Project is located on ~92,829 acres in Virginia and West Virginia. The property was formerly owned by TFG, an independent TIMO, which had a fiduciary responsibility to provide long-term financial returns to investors through the management of forest resources. In 2022, the property was acquired by Aurora Sustainable Lands LLC (Aurora), a company specifically created to manage forestlands for climate outcomes and derive profits from carbon markets in lieu of aggressive timber activities. By enrolling this land in a carbon project, Aurora will commit the project area to a management strategy that generates the majority of income from carbon credit generation as opposed to commercial harvesting for timber products. The property contains multiple high conservation value sites and several endangered species. It is home to a WV State Record Yellow Poplar, a prized old-growth tree that demonstrates the climate storage potential of the region.

ACR0873.description: Trailhead Ventures, LLC purchased three Mississippi River islands in May 2022 with the primary purpose of developing forest carbon projects that conserve and restore the area to a natural forested state. The islands contain a significant amount of forested wetland areas which help purify the river and serve migratory birds/pollinators along the Mississippi Flyway. In a scenario without carbon credit revenue, an independent Certified Forester determined that much of the project area would be clearcut. The landowner would be incentivized to clearcut due to significant timber revenue in the short-term, and long-term the clearcut would allow higher timber value shade intolerant species to dominate over low timber value shade tolerant species. With the carbon project, conservation and growth of the forests will be maximized.

ACR0880.methodology: ACR Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Non-Federal U.S. Forestlands

The values and uses of the Ashland County Forest have and will continue to contribute significantly to fulfilling many of the region's ecological and socioeconomic needs through uses such as outdoor recreation, hunting, timber harvest, and providing essential wildlife habitat. Escalating operational costs and reduced funding are increasing the reliance on timber harvests to fund County services and demand for forest products remains strong. By cutting less than is currently allowed under their management plan and committing to maintaining forest stocks above current onsite volumes, the project will enhance climate benefits through carbon sequestration as the sale of carbon credits will displace the increased need for additional timber revenues.

ACR0881.methodology: ACR Capturing and Destroying Methane from Coal and Trona Mines in North America
ACR0881.description: The project activity will gather, collect, and capture coal mine methane that otherwise would be vented to the atmosphere and inject the collected methane into a pipeline for offsite beneficial use. The methane this project will capture is fugitive methane emissions from a gob vent borehole that are the result of previous and completed longwall coal mining and the disruption of the natural shale barriers that kept the methane underground and sequestered. As a result of coal mining, this methane now needs to be removed from the subsurface atmosphere in a controlled fashion to prevent future venting of methane.

ACR0890.methodology: ACR Plugging of Orphaned Oil and Gas (OOG) Wells
ACR0890.description: Six orphaned oil and gas wells were plugged in Washington County, Ok. Each of the six wells were officially documented as orphaned wells with the Oklahoma Corporation Commission. The wells had not sold hydrocarbons for many years and were leaking methane to the atmosphere. The wells posed health and well-being risks to the landowners and threatened proximal natural resources. As of May 2023, there were over 17,000 documented orphaned wells in Oklahoma. Over the past decade, the Oklahoma State Funds Plugging Program has plugged an average of ~140 orphaned wells per year. At this rate, even with additional federal funds, state-allocated resources are not available to plug growing inventory in any reasonable timeframe. Rebellion Energy Solutions, the project developer, quantified the leaking methane, took responsibility for the wells for the purpose of proper plugging and remediation, and confirmed total methane abatement post-plugging. The project is mapped to several UN SDGs.

ACR0891.methodology: ACR Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Non-Federal U.S. Forestlands
ACR0891.description: The Grace Woodlands property is a member-owned 10,000 acre wilderness playground located in the nationally-important Chesapeake Bay Watershed. In close proximity to the Washington D.C metropolitan area, these carbon-rich forests face heightened risk of land conversion, maintaining and sequestering additional carbon in a highly biodiverse region that provides climate resilient habitat for threatened and endangered species. The land in the Grace Woodlands IFM project consists of intact mixed hardwood forest that provides species connectivity through essential wildlife corridors and climate resilience with its unique topography, both above and belowground. It also helps protect regional water quality and provides access to iconic and beloved outdoor recreation areas. Through its dedicated landowners, the project supports long-term stewardship of these priority forests.

ACR0900.methodology: ACR Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Non-Federal U.S. Forestlands
ACR0900.description: The NativState - Calion Ouachita River Wilderness Forest Carbon Program is the largest private land conservation project in Arkansas to date. With 36,482 acres of nearly contiguous bottomland hardwoods conserved along the Ouachita River bottoms, it is truly in a league of its own. Native bottomland hardwood forests will be managed for sustainable use and protection of biodiversity with a unified commitment to maintaining forest CO2e stocks through certified sustainable forest management. Calion forests are located in the West Gulf Coastal Plain ecoregion of Arkansas along the Ouachita River bottoms where, prior to European settlement, the Coastal Plain may have had the greatest landscape-level biodiversity of any ecoregion in Arkansas. Implementation of the carbon project presents an exciting opportunity to conserve these native forests and protect biodiversity, minimize disturbance, accelerate carbon sequestration, and improve wildlife habitat.

ACR0901.methodology: ARB Compliance Offset Protocol: U.S. Forest Projects

In 2022, the property was acquired by BSFC, a company specifically created to manage forestlands for climate outcomes and derive profits from carbon markets in lieu of aggressive timber activities. By enrolling this land in a carbon project, BSFC will commit the project area to a management strategy that generates the majority of income from carbon credit generation as opposed to commercial harvesting for timber products. The property provides habitat for a wide variety of sensitive flora and fauna, including the Northern Goshawk, Eastern Massasauga and Salamander Mussel.

Project management activities will serve to protect forest habitat and species found within the project area - including the threatened Canada Lynx. ACR0958.methodology: ACR Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Non-Federal U.S. Forestlands
ACR0958.description: The Hood River County Tree Farm extends from the north slopes of Mt. Hood towards the Columbia River in Oregon. The Tree Farm is managed primarily for the production and sale of forest products. Timber sales are a critical source of revenue for the County; harvests contribute 33 percent of the annual general fund revenue. Recent reductions in other revenue sources, including from the cessation of federal timber harvests and state laws restricting property taxation, combined with increasing costs of providing public services, have put the Tree Farm's carbon stocks at risk. Rather than increase per acre harvest rates to generate needed revenue, the County will use carbon revenues to purchase additional timberland to help it meet budget needs. Through this carbon project, Hood River County is locking in a forest management regime that balances carbon sequestration with other management priorities, rather than pursuing a more aggressive harvesting regime and reducing carbon stocks.

ACR0982.description: The Anew - Linkletter Forestry Project is located on about 41,000 acres across 5 counties in central Maine and owned by two family businesses, Linkletter Timberlands LLC and Linkletter & Sons. This land was acquired over the past 30 years, and the ownership has expanded over time as the family's investments in the forest products industry has generated profit. By enrolling this land in a carbon project, the landowners will commit the project area to a management strategy that generates income from carbon credit generation in lieu of commercial timber products.

ACR0983.methodology: ACR Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Non-Federal U.S. Forestlands
ACR0983.description: The Shamrock Ranch Sustainable Forestry Project encompasses a total area of 17,050 acres (with forest cover of 13,626 acres), with approximately 80% of the land consisting of forested areas. This project is situated in Mendocino County, Northern California. The property predominately includes Madrone, Black Oak and Oregon White Oak with some mix of Douglas fir, Coastal Oak Woodland, Blue Oak Woodland and Montane Chaparral. The Shamrock Ranch is home to a large, trophy caliber population of the rare Tule Elk, as well as abundant trophy class blacktail deer, large flocks of wild turkeys and great numbers of wild Russian boar. The mission at the ranch is to find a harmonious balance between conservation efforts and business development by making the cash flow break even.

ACR0984.methodology: ACR Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Non-Federal U.S. Forestlands
ACR0984.description: The Anew - Eau Claire County Forestry Project is located on 48,510 acres of northern hardwood, aspen, and oak forest in central Wisconsin. The County has practiced intensive commercial timber management across its ownership since 1933 with timbering revenues representing one of the largest sources of annual income for the County. Challenged by funding issues from increasing demand for services and rising operational costs, the County has considered further increasing harvesting to fill the budget gap. Revenue generated from a carbon project will help alleviate these financial pressures and accelerate Eau Claire County toward their goal of becoming carbon neutral by 2050.

ACR0988.methodology: ACR Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Non-Federal U.S. Forestlands
ACR0988.description: The Anew - Sawyer County Forestry Project is located on a mixture of northern hardwood, aspen, and conifer forestlands across 105,445 acres. The values and uses of the County Forest have and will continue to contribute significantly to fulfilling many of the region's ecological and socioeconomic needs through uses such as outdoor recreation, hunting, timber harvest, and providing essential wildlife habitat. Escalating operational costs and reduced funding are increasing the reliance on timber harvests to fund County services and demand for forest products remains strong. By cutting less than is currently allowed under their management plan and committing to maintaining forest stocks above current onsite volumes, the project will enhance climate benefits through carbon sequestration as the sale of carbon credits will displace the increased need for additional timber revenues.

ACR1002.methodology: ACR Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Non-Federal U.S. Forestlands
ACR1002.description: Doyon, Limited's carbon forest offset project, Doyon Ts'oo, is located near the rural communities of Circle, Eagle, Stevens Village in Southeast Interior Alaska, and Huslia in Northwest Interior Alaska along the Yukon and Koyukuk River, and the Steese and Taylor Highway. Ts'oo translates to 'spruce tree' in Hans Gwitchin, one of the indigenous languages within the project area that spans across continuous boreal forest located on Doyon, Limited-owned land. As the largest private landowner in Alaska, Doyon, Limited is prioritizing forest health, fuel mitigation, and responsible forest management to create resilient forests over time. The development of an Improved Forest Management carbon project places focus on preserving the pristine forestland in this area of our region while highlighting the ecological and cultural values of our lands and creating in-region economic benefits for current and future generations.

By employing practices of sustainable forestry and maintenance of forest carbon stocking, this project will achieve positive climate impacts.

ACR1006.methodology: ACR Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Non-Federal U.S. Forestlands
ACR1006.description: The Challenge Tree Farm IFM project is composed of approximately 8,500 acres of Sierra Nevada mixed conifer/hardwood forest that will be managed for increased carbon sequestration by restricting harvesting to rates less than growth over the project term. This will be achieved by increasing rotation lengths relative to common practice standards in the region and by proactively applying thinning and fuels reduction treatments that accelerate the development of larger diameter trees and reduce catastrophic wildfire risk. The future planned harvest levels are well below the legally allowable levels provided for under the California Forest Practice Rules.

ACR1010.methodology: ACR Plugging of Orphaned Oil and Gas (OOG) Wells
ACR1010.description: Five orphaned oil and gas wells carrying the official orphaned status/designation at the state level were identified in Adams County, CO as continuously leaking methane from the wellhead. Pre-plugging leak rates will be quantified, after which Carbon Shield will plug and abandon each well per the Colorado ECMC rules and regulations providing permanent abatement of the fugitive emissions. Post-plugging measurements will then be collected to confirm that emissions from the plugged wells have been fully abated.

ACR1014.methodology: ACR Certified Reclaimed HFC Refrigerants, Propellants, and Fire Suppressants
ACR1014.description: Fielding Environmental ("Fielding") is one of only two major refrigerant reclamation and recycling companies in Canada. Refrigerant reclamation and recycling is a core business unit for Fielding and it includes ODS and non-ODS refrigerants that come from various sectors across the country including the automotive sector and the refrigeration and air conditioning sector. Fielding receives refrigerants from authorized wholesalers or directly from contractors and end-users that have collected refrigerant from end-of-life equipment or after equipment retrofits. Through an innovative and customized process Fielding reclaims refrigerants, which are then sold back into the refrigerant market, avoiding the use of an equivalent volume of virgin refrigerants, and their eventual GHG emissions.

ACR1031.description: The Burnett County Timberlands IFM project consists of 95,000 forested acres in northwest Wisconsin. Burnett County manages their forest to optimize and sustain the forest's utility via the production of forest products, recreational opportunities, wildlife habitat and watershed protection. The local community is dependent on the forest to generate timber revenues to offset local taxes and fund a portion of the local county government. Carbon revenue will help diversify existing forest-based revenues, providing additional certainty and assistance with county budgeting for the next two decades. With the initiation of an IFM project, forest carbon sequestration and storage has been incorporated as a primary management goal.

ACR1037.methodology: ACR Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Non-Federal U.S. Forestlands
ACR1037.description: The Thompson Family Forest Restoration Project is located in north-central Oregon, approximately 15 miles southeast of Heppner, and includes 9,442 acres. The area primarily consists of pine and fir tree species of younger to medium ages resulting from decades of industrial forest management. The project will achieve GHG removals by enhancing the forest's health and resilience through thinning, harvesting less than annual growth – extending the rotation age, and managing a mix of species that can adapt to climate change. The result of these management actions will increase the forest's capacity to remove and store carbon over time, surpassing common forestry practices, and reduce the risk of stand-replacing wildfires within the project area. The resulting forest will be a mix of larger, older well-spaced healthy and resilient trees that will be adaptable to a changing climate with enhanced habitat for native fish and wildlife species.

Per the Methodology, "reclamation and use" of certified reclaimed HFC refrigerant refers specifically to the production of such refrigerant and the subsequent sale, title transfer or return to a refrigerant distributor, refrigerant wholesaler, or end-user (either through direct sale, title transfer or return to an end user or through installation conducted via service technician) for use in refrigeration or air conditioning equipment. ACR1050.methodology: ACR Certified Reclaimed HFC Refrigerants, Propellants, and Fire Suppressants
ACR1050.description: The American Refrigerants HFC Reclamation Project - 2023 (the Project) recovers previously used, reclaimed hydrofluorocarbons (HFC) to be used in place of newly produced, virgin HFCs either in new refrigeration or air conditioning equipment or to recharge existing equipment. By eliminating the need for virgin HFC that would otherwise be manufactured to meet the demand, American Refrigerants, Inc. (AR) (the Project Proponent) is ensuring that no additional HFC will leak into the atmosphere, besides what has already been produced. At AR reclamation facility in Bradenton, Florida, recovered refrigerants are received from across the United States, oil and water impurities are removed and the recovered refrigerant are restores to the AHRI 700 Standard for Specification for Fluorocarbon Refrigerants. The reclaimed refrigerants are then sold to distributors, service companies and wholesalers located in the United States.

The timberland has been managed for multiple uses for generations, with a focus on sustained yield and a healthy forest ecosystem. ACR1054.methodology: ACR Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Non-Federal U.S. Forestlands
ACR1054.description: This project is located in the Olympic Peninsula within Clallam County on 4,410 acres. This IFM project will increase forest carbon stocking during the project period beyond local common practice. This will be achieved by expanding voluntary riparian buffers, reducing the intensity of silvicultural practices, and increasing rotation ages via FSC-certified management practices. Management activities will include some precommercial and commercial thinning and even aged management with retention, which will create a mix of mature and young forests with native trees species. These efforts will result in an increase in forest carbon accumulation over the project lifetime. The management regime will also improve overall forest health and resiliency while creating and enhancing habitat for fish and wildlife species. Carbon revenues will replace some forgone timber revenue and support EFM's overarching vision of developing a protected, resilient, and functional working landscape.

ACR1141.methodology: ACR Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Non-Federal U.S. Forestlands
ACR1141.description: The Cascades Forestry Project is a land stewardship program operated by Columbia Land Trust, whose mission is to conserve and care for the lands, waters, and wildlife of the Columbia River region. The region served by this project follows the lower Columbia River for 230 miles through Oregon and Washington, in an area stretching from The Dalles to the Pacific Ocean though several diverse ecoregions. Through the Cascades Forestry Project, the Land Trust is transitioning key forests in the Columbia River watershed from intensive private and industrial management to carbon- and landscape-focused stewardship. By developing this forest carbon project using ACR's Programmatic Development Approach, the proponent can respond to carbon market incentives by adding newly acquired sites over time. The Cascades Forestry project currently encompasses approximately 3,000 acres and the project development team has an ambitious five-year goal of increasing the project impact to 7,000 acres or more.

ACR1142.methodology: ACR Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Non-Federal U.S. Forestlands
ACR1142.siteLocation: Olympic Peninsula - Clallam and Jefferson counties
ACR1142.description: This 60,000-acre IFM carbon project is located on private forestland in Washington's Olympic Peninsula. EFM's goal is to remove one million tonnes of carbon emissions over the next decade by transitioning the area through carbon-smart management practices. This will involve enhancing timber quality, producing larger and more valuable logs, and delivering long-term benefits including increased carbon storage, salmon habitat restoration, recreational opportunities, and support for non-timber products and cultural harvesting by tribes. The project will increase forest carbon stocks beyond regional norms by implementing enhanced riparian buffers, adopting less intensive forestry techniques, and extending the rotation age under FSC-certified practices. Management will involve a mix of pre-commercial and commercial thinning and even-aged management with retention, fostering a diverse forest landscape, thereby enhancing carbon accumulation.

ACR1143.methodology: ACR Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Non-Federal U.S. Forestlands
ACR1143.description: The Anew - Elliott State Research Forest Project is one of a few innovative carbon reduction and removal projects developed on state forest lands. The Elliott State Research Forest covers ~83,000 acres and spans the Coos, Lower Umpqua, and Tenmile watersheds in southern Oregon near the Pacific Coast. The native forest type features a mosaic of western redcedar, western hemlock, Sitka spruce and Douglas fir, though the current forest composition is largely influenced by past, intensive management regimes oriented around Douglas fir plantations. The project will provide significant climate benefits through carbon sequestration via sustainable forest management and carbon stored in long lived wood products. Project development will also supplement the forest's multiple use outcomes like biodiversity protection, recreation, scientific research, and enhancing economic and cultural values

ACR1144.methodology: ACR Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Non-Federal U.S. Forestlands
ACR1144.description: The Mountainy Pond Forests project covers 5,400 acres, mostly in Dedham, Maine. The forest has historically been managed parcel-by-parcel under an opportunistic harvesting regime to fund land ownership expenses, which have steadily increased over time resulting in greater harvest pressure. Under the carbon project, forest management will be guided by a new ownership-wide plan focused on ecosystem health and climate mitigation. The project proponent plans to replace the existing series of disjointed management plans (one for each tract) with a single ATFS certified plan that operates at a landscape scale for long-term planning. The project proponent expects to reduce harvesting substantially over the carbon project term if a reduction in harvest revenues can be supported by carbon pricing. The baseline for this project will be constrained to observed harvest intensity on similar ownerships using the ACR Comparable Properties Analysis Tool.

ACR1145.methodology: ACR Plugging of Orphaned Oil and Gas (OOG) Wells
ACR1145.description: The project activity is the plugging of orphan wells in Oklahoma. Each of the wells in the project has been documented as orphaned wells by the Oklahoma Corporation Commission. These wells leak methane into the atmosphere. Additionally, orphan wells pose health and well-being risks to the landowners and threaten proximal natural resources. Rebellion Energy Solutions, the project developer, is responsible for these wells for the purpose of proper plugging and remediation. Methane leaking from orphan oil and gas wells is to be mitigated via the permanent plugging of wellbores. Methane abatement is confirmed post-plugging. Land restoration is voluntarily paid for and conducted by Rebellion Energy Solutions in and around well sites. The purpose of this project is to reduce the fugitive methane emissions that were and would have been generated by the wells in question in the scenario that wells are not plugged.

ACR1166.methodology: ACR Plugging of Orphaned Oil and Gas (OOG) Wells
ACR1166.description: Across America—especially in the Great Plains—countless orphaned wells are leaking methane, a potent greenhouse gas. These wells not only contribute significantly to climate change but also threaten groundwater and pose safety risks to local communities. Methane traps heat over 80 times more effectively than CO2 in the short term, making it a top target for immediate climate action. AMR Holdings, LLC is tackling this issue by identifying and safely plugging these wells. This process eliminates methane emissions, protects water resources, and restores surrounding land. AMR begins with methane testing, followed by permanent well closure and site restoration. Focusing first on Oklahoma, AMR is reducing emissions one well at a time. Our mission: cut methane from orphaned wells, restore damaged land, safeguard water, and lead in sustainable resource management—making a measurable impact in the fight against climate change.

Current and future management of the land base will have a range of management objectives but will exclude the harvesting of timber for a minimum of 20 years. The Project Participant's management provides significant recreational, ecological, and environmental benefits, including the maintenance of forest and wildlife habitat.

ACR1222.methodology: ACR Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Canadian Forestlands
ACR1222.description: The Eastern Forests - Yellow Gate Acadian Forests Project is an Improved Forest Management (IFM) project focused on the restoration of natural ecological conditions to promote resilient and biodiverse forests on 2,000 hectares of multi-generational private lands in southeastern, New Brunswick. This project will focus on the implementation of IFM activities such as silvicultural practices prioritizing carbon sequestration and forest restoration to facilitate the generation of both avoided emissions and removals to support climate change mitigation. Project lands will be managed long-term under a sustainable Forest Management Plan with reduced harvest levels and carbon-focused silviculture to store and sequester carbon beyond baseline levels.

ACR1223.methodology: ACR Afforestation and Reforestation of Degraded Lands
ACR1223.description: The Northern Cheyenne Reforestation project supports the goals of the Northern Cheyenne Tribe in reforesting forestland degraded by a series of wildfires on the Northern Cheyenne Reservation in southeast Montana. Through this project, the Tribe and its partner, The Climate Trust, are working to reforest 15,000 acres or more, and re-establish forest stands to be managed sustainably under the Northern Cheyenne Tribe's Integrated Resource Management Plan.  The project activities include tree planting and any related site preparation or post-establishment silvicultural treatments to improve seedling survival and growth.

ACR1225.methodology: ACR Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Non-Federal U.S. Forestlands
ACR1225.description: Located in north-central Mississippi, the Double Springs Forest Carbon project covers more than 50,000 acres of sustainably-managed forestland. The project will provide climate benefits through practices to increase on-site carbon storage and climate resiliency, such as extension of rotation age and a reduction in harvest intensity. Activities will serve to protect habitat and species found within the project area - including a rare bald cypress-swamp tupelo forest, and habitat for the federally endangered red-cockaded woodpecker. The property is dual-certified under the Sustainable Forestry Initiative (SFI) and the Forest Stewardship Council (FSC), and primarily consists of loblolly pine forests and hardwood bottomlands.

ACR1230.methodology: ACR Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Canadian Forestlands
ACR1230.description: The Anew - Harrison Forestry Project spans 10,000 hectares in Cumberland County, Nova Scotia. By committing to maintain forest C02 stocks through sustainable management, the project will provide significant climate benefits through carbon sequestration.

ACR1233.methodology: ACR Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Non-Federal U.S. Forestlands
ACR1233.description: The Florence County Timberlands project consists of over 30,000 forested acres in northeast Wisconsin. Florence County optimizes their forest's utility via the production of forest products, recreation, wildlife habitat and watershed protection. With the initiation of an IFM project, climate change mitigation has been incorporated as a primary management goal. The County Forest is shaped by past exploitative logging and land-use practices. With the support of the carbon project, the County Forest is now managed for climate mitigation and sustaining health, productivity, and biodiversity. Carbon credit revenue will contribute to community services funded by the County budget and will diversify income sources, providing additional financial stability for improved forest stewardship over the coming decades. The project utilizes a dynamic baseline assessment framework and a GIS-based Comparable Properties Analysis to demonstrate additionality throughout the project term.

ACR1235.methodology: ACR Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Canadian Forestlands
ACR1235.description: The Anew - Claybelt Forestry Project takes place on 52,061 hectares of forestland near Timmins, Ontario. Through sustainable forestry practices, the project will maintain and sequester carbon throughout the project life.

ACR1236.methodology: ACR Certified Reclaimed HFC Refrigerants, Propellants, and Fire Suppressants
ACR1236.description: The voluntary emission reduction project was undertaken to encourage the recovery of used HFCs and to avoid production of virgin HFCs through reclamation. The HFCs in this project were domestically sourced in the U.S. and reclaimed to industry standards at A-Gas facilities with the intention to re-sell into the market. All applicable laws and regulations were followed throughout this project.

ACR1237.methodology: ACR Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Canadian Forestlands
ACR1237.description: Finite Carbon – Wikwemikong First Nation IFM is located on Wikwemikong Unceded Territory on the eastern peninsula of Manitoulin Island, Ontario, encompassing approximately 45,606 hectares of forestland. Prior to the project, lands were managed for periodic commercial timber harvesting. The project implements a modified management regime that reduces harvest intensity and delays harvest timing relative to this baseline, increasing long-term forest carbon stocks through extended rotations, retention of mature trees and standing deadwood, and selective stand improvement. Carbon revenue enables the land manager to forego a portion of harvestable timber value. The project occurs on lands governed by the Wikwemikong Unceded Territory First Nation, whose long-term stewardship reduces land conversion risk and supports permanence. Community members will be involved with monitoring and inventory. The project also supports cultural land uses consistent with First Nations stewardship.

ACR1238.methodology: ACR Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Non-Federal U.S. Forestlands
ACR1238.description: Dixon-Moody Family Forests is an IFM project developed by Real Heritage Group located in southern Alabama and northern Florida on fifth-generation family forestlands. The project applies extended rotation ages, reduced harvest intensity, and sustainable forest management practices to increase long-term forest carbon stocks and deliver durable carbon removals and reductions. As the project ramps to more than 8,000 acres, it will serve to enhance water quality, conserve biodiversity, and strengthen the ecological integrity of working family forests, including the restoration of historically native longleaf pine systems.

ACR1239.methodology: ACR Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Non-Federal U.S. Forestlands
ACR1239.description: The North Woods Carbon Project is located on privately owned forestland in northern Maine and managed by Allagash Timberlands LP. The Project covers 61,207 hectares of mixed, tolerant hardwood–dominated forest and is designed to increase forest carbon storage by deferring planned timber harvests in mixed hardwood stands. By allowing trees to grow for longer periods, the forest accumulates additional biomass, resulting in increased removal of CO2 from the atmosphere and greater long-term carbon storage. This approach represents a voluntary change from business-as-usual forest management, under which these stands would be harvested for timber production. The primary objective of the Project is to increase net GHG removals beyond what would occur under typical management practices by retaining forest carbon stocks over time. In addition to climate benefits, the Project supports the conservation of hardwood forests that provide important wildlife habitat and promotes long-term forest health and resilience.

Per the Methodology, "reclamation and use" of certified reclaimed HFC refrigerant refers specifically to the production of such refrigerant and the subsequent sale, title transfer or return to a refrigerant distributor, refrigerant wholesaler, or end-user (either through direct sale, title transfer or return to an end user or through installation conducted via service technician) for use in refrigeration or air conditioning equipment. ACR1247.methodology: ACR Certified Reclaimed HFC Refrigerants, Propellants, and Fire Suppressants
ACR1247.description: The American Refrigerants HFC Reclamation Project - 2025 (the Project) recovers previously used, reclaimed hydrofluorocarbons (HFC) to be used in place of newly produced, virgin HFCs either in new refrigeration or air conditioning equipment or to recharge existing equipment. By eliminating the need for virgin HFC that would otherwise be manufactured to meet the demand, American Refrigerants, Inc. (AR) (the Project Proponent) is ensuring that no additional HFC will leak into the atmosphere, besides what has already been produced. At AR reclamation facility in Bradenton, Florida, recovered refrigerants are received from across the United States, oil and water impurities are removed and the recovered refrigerant are restores to the AHRI 700 Standard for Specification for Fluorocarbon Refrigerants. The reclaimed refrigerants are then sold to distributors, service companies and wholesalers located in the United States.

ACR1249.methodology: ACR Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Non-Federal U.S. Forestlands
ACR1249.description: NativState - North Central Louisiana IFM Carbon Removal Project is a large-scale private land conservation initiative spanning approximately 52,000 acres of contiguous forestland in central Louisiana, just north of Kisatchie National Forest. This project is structured as an IFM removals-only carbon program, meaning that credited climate benefits are derived exclusively from increases in onsite forest carbon stocks relative to baseline conditions. Through the implementation of improved management practices, the project will enhance standing biomass, promote forest growth, and increase long-term carbon storage across the project area. These forests will be managed under certified sustainable forestry practices designed to increase net carbon sequestration over time through improved forest management activities, including extended rotations, reduced harvest intensity, and optimization of stand structure. Situated within Gulf Coastal Plain, the project provides important habitat connectivity for native wildlife.
