GS23229.description: The 240 MW Khizi-Absheron Wind Power Plant Project is Azerbaijan's first international investment-based independent wind power project and the largest in the Caucasus region, making it a first-of-its-kind in the country. Located 45 km northwest of Baku, it consists of Zone 1 – Area 1 with 78 MW in the Absheron region and Zone 2 – Khizi 3 with 162.5 MW in the Khizi region. The project will supply electricity to the national grid, with Azerenergy OJSC as the offtaker.

GS23232.description: The Real Case VPA aims to restore unutilized or unmanaged degraded areas into biodiverse forests using multiple native tree species through restoration techniques, such as reforestation, enrichment planting, assisted natural regeneration, and community-based agroforestry. The project includes activities targeting fire management and prevention, forest protection, community capacity-building and development so to achieve broader social and environmental goals of the ICCs/IPs.

GS23233.description: The project, Summit Carbon Solutions – Capture, Transport, and Storage of CO2 from the Fermentation of Biomass (the "Project") quantifies emission removals generated by the project activity, which involves the capture and permanent sequestration of biogenic carbon dioxide (CO2) from 57 ethanol and feed production facilities and 1 proposed Sustainable Aviation Fuel production facility ("biorefineries") in secure geologic storage complex(es).

GS23234.methodology: AMS-II.E. Energy efficiency and fuel switching measures for buildings
GS23234.description: The purpose of the voluntary project activity (VPA) "Greening by insulating for low income housing in NY" is to improve the energy efficiency of existing buildings in New York State by implementing one or a combination of energy efficiency measures in a building. These may include, but are not limited to, improving thermal performance through insulation, efficient lighting systems, efficient heating, proper ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) systems.

GS23235.methodology: GS Methodology for Afforestation/Reforestation GHG Emissions Reduction and Sequestration
GS23235.description: The agroforestry project located  in different districts of Odisha.

GS23236.methodology: GS Methodology for Metered and Measured Energy Cooking Devices
GS23236.description: The proposed project aims to reduce fuelwood consumption by replacing inefficient traditional cookstoves and LPG stoves with energy-efficient induction stoves in Kerala, India. The initiative plans to distribute induction cookstoves to 100,000 households. This project seeks to improve both environmental sustainability and public health by offering a cleaner, safer, and more efficient cooking alternative.

GS23239.methodology: GS Methodology for emission reductions from safe drinking water supply
GS23239.description:
The primary objective of this project is to enhance access to clean and safe drinking water for both institutions and communities across Rwanda through the installation of Water purification systems (Water ATMs). By installing these Water ATMs, the project aims to provide a sustainable and affordable solution for safe drinking water, reducing reliance on unsafe water sources and minimizing health risks associated with waterborne diseases such as cholera, dysentery, typhoid etc. It also reduces the burden of water collection, particularly for women and girls, allowing them to focus on education and economic opportunities. 

The project supports environmental conservation by reducing the need to boil water with firewood or charcoal, thereby lowering energy consumption, deforestation, and Greenhouse gas emissions. By ensuring reliable access to clean drinking water, this initiative promotes public health, economic growth, and social well-being, contributing to sustainable development and strengthening community resilience.

GS23240.methodology: GS Methodology for emission reductions from safe drinking water supply
GS23240.description:
The primary objective of this project is to enhance access to clean and safe drinking water for both institutions and communities across Rwanda through the installation of Water purification systems (Water ATMs). By installing these Water ATMs, the project aims to provide a sustainable and affordable solution for safe drinking water, reducing reliance on unsafe water sources and minimizing health risks associated with waterborne diseases such as cholera, dysentery, typhoid etc. It also reduces the burden of water collection, particularly for women and girls, allowing them to focus on education and economic opportunities. 

The project supports environmental conservation by reducing the need to boil water with firewood or charcoal, thereby lowering energy consumption, deforestation, and Greenhouse gas emissions. By ensuring reliable access to clean drinking water, this initiative promotes public health, economic growth, and social well-being, contributing to sustainable development and strengthening community resilience.

GS23241.methodology: AMS-III.F. Avoidance of methane emissions through composting
GS23241.description:
KOFERT ORGANIC SRL is developing an innovative project in Baicoi, Prahova County, to produce solid organic fertilizer using 100% natural materials. The project aims to expand the capacity of the existing composting plant, recovering organic waste through aerobic fermentation, contributing to sustainable agriculture and environmental protection.

By utilizing Japanese Kohshin KNLL-6000 SHW technology, the plant ensures efficient and accelerated composting of animal manure, transforming it into a stable, granular, and hygienic fertilizer. The high-temperature process eliminates pathogens and prevents seed germination in the compost.

The resulting organic fertilizer is rich in essential nutrients and organic matter, with a balanced pH that enhances soil structure and water retention. Its use helps reduce atmospheric carbon and supports sustainable farming practices.

Through this project, KOFERT ORGANIC SRL provides a sustainable solution for managing organic waste and improving soil quality, strengthening partnerships with livestock farms and agricultural enterprises.

GS23242.description:
KOFERT ORGANIC SRL is developing an organic fertilizer production project in Mihăilești, Giurgiu County, using advanced Japanese Kohshin composting lines type KNLL-6000 SHW technology. The process involves aerobic fermentation of poultry manure and organic waste, ensuring a stable, hygienic, and nutrient-rich fertilizer.

The project will be implemented in phases, starting with the installation of a composting line, followed by an expansion to increase processing capacity. The facility will also include sorting and packaging lines for various product formats. The technology ensures efficient manure processing, eliminating pathogens and preventing seed germination while maintaining high-quality organic content.

The final product is a balanced organic fertilizer enriched with essential nutrients, improving soil structure, enhancing water retention, and supporting sustainable agriculture. By promoting carbon sequestration and increasing soil fertility, this initiative contributes to environmental sustainability while offering an effective solution for managing livestock waste and improving agricultural productivity.

GS23243.methodology: AMS-III.AU. Methane emission reduction by adjusted water management practice in rice cultivation
GS23243.description: Agriculture sector is the second highest contributor to total greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions in Cambodia and rice cultivation is one of the main GHG sources. The project plans to introduce AWD method to rice farmers to reduce methane emissions related with rice cultivation. Sansom Mlup Prey Organization (SMP), local partner to the project; is working on building capacity on agriculture, providing technical support to more than four thousand farmers and their families who are living in and around eight wildlife sanctuaries across six provinces such as Prash Vihear, Stung Treng, Mondulkiri, Rathanakiri Kampong Thom, and Siem Reap in Cambodia.

GS23244.description: The purpose of the VPA is to disseminate Safe Water Supply (SWS) devices such as Household Water Treatment (HWT) technologies in domestic households and communities of western regions of Uganda, Africa. They have planned to distribute water purification system (WPS) to households which were earlier using wood on rudimentary stoves for boiling water or were consuming untreated water. The project makes the end-users energy efficient and reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions otherwise resulting from the burning of non-renewable woody biomass for boiling unsafe water to make it safe for consumption. The project boundary is the geographical boundary of western Uganda where the water filters are proposed to be distributed. The VPA will be implemented by SPOUTS International (SPOUTS) who are Project Owners whereas AGS Carbon Advisory is the Coordinating/Managing Entity (CME) of the PoA. SPOUTS will implement the project with support from AERA Group and in partnership with local partners and would ensure the last-mile distribution/installation of the water purification systems (WPS) to the beneficiaries.

GS23245.methodology: AMS-III.AU. Methane emission reduction by adjusted water management practice in rice cultivation
GS23245.developer: Sow and Reap Agro Private Limited
GS23245.description: The project reduces methane (CH4) emissions by implementing improved water management practices, specifically the Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) method in paddy fields. AWD has been proven to lower CH4 emissions by up to 48% compared to continuously flooded conditions, where anaerobic decomposition of organic matter results in high methane emissions.

GS23246.methodology: GS Methodology for Metered and Measured Energy Cooking Devices
GS23246.description:
Household air pollution is a global crisis and India is not unaffected by the problem. There is significant dependence on polluting traditional cookstoves for cooking in rural and semi-urban households in the country. Household pollution can cause diseases and women are particularly affected due to their direct exposure to cooking fires and involvement in daily cooking. Combustion of non-renewable fuels and the release of greenhouse gas emissions into the environment adds to the global warming problem. 

The proposed project activity will address this problem by distributing induction stoves to the target households in Kerela, India. The purpose of the project activity is to decrease fuel wood consumption by replacing inefficient traditional cookstoves and LPG stoves in 1,00,000 households with efficient induction stoves starting with pilot of 1000 Induction cookstove deployment.

GS23249.developer: GAİA CLİMATE FİNANSAL DANIŞMANLIK HİZMETLERİ VE TİCARET ANONİM ŞİRKETİ
GS23249.description: The NAVOI-1-2 Solar Power Plant Project is a large-scale renewable energy initiative designed to support Uzbekistan's transition toward clean energy and contribute to the global effort to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. The purpose of the project is to generate electricity by using clean solar power resources to meet the national electricity demand. The expected annual GHG emission reductions over the first crediting period are 554,070 tCO2e/yr, that will contribute to the alleviation of climate change effects. NAVOI-1-2 Solar Power Plant will contribute to the achievement of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy), SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth) and SDG 13 (Climate Action).

GS23250.description:
Lagos has around 4.7 million gensets, which emit an estimated 39 million tonnes of CO2 per year. The reliance on gensets for electricity due to insufficient grid availability leads to health issues and costs Nigerians ₦7.6 trillion on fuel and maintenance. The average small to medium business spends ~₦50,000-400,000 per month just on fuel.

This is not just an energy crisis. It is a missed opportunity for economic growth, environmental sustainability, and global leadership.

Earthbond, a climate tech start-up based in Lagos, is implementing a distributed solar project in Nigeria to reduce reliance on expensive and polluting gensets. Earthbond provides a digital one-stop-shop which removes the complexity and cost for over 45 million African businesses who need to switch to clean, affordable, and reliable energy.
As well as the economic and health benefits, solar installations and the displacement of gensets will lead to a reduction in CO2 emissions. 

The technology includes solar PV systems which are suitable for micro, small and medium sized enterprises (MSMEs). The project aims to reach thousands of businesses across Nigeria and will last for 15 years.

The Earthbond Distributed Solar project will create significant economic, social and environmental impact by reducing the costs associated with electricity supply, remove exposure to smoke and carbon monoxide, and reduce CO2 emissions.

GS23252.description:
The Niger Delta Community-Driven Mangrove Restoration Project is a scalable initiative focused on restoring the historically mangrove-rich wetlands of the Niger Delta through a community-led approach.

The Niger Delta—the largest river delta in Africa and home to the world's third-largest mangrove forest—has faced severe degradation over the past decades due to a variety of pressures. This has compromised biodiversity, diminished livelihoods, and increased vulnerability to flooding and erosion for the 30 million people who live there.

This Programme of Activities aims to restore the ecosystem through training local communities to plant native, locally adapted mangrove species, while also addressing the causes of mangrove loss.

Its objectives are to: 
• Empower communities by providing the livelihood support, education, and tools needed to become long-term ecosystem stewards and bolster their resilience in a climate-changing world, 
• Restore a critical ecosystem and its services while promoting biodiversity by rebuilding the habitats of numerous species, strengthening regional food security, and providing flood and storm protection. 
• And finally, sequester carbon in the fight against climate change while utilizing mangroves as a powerful nature-based solution.

Rooted in strong local partnerships and ecosystem restoration approaches, the project is designed to scale and serve as a model for community-first restoration across Nigeria and the wider region.

GS23253.methodology: GS Methodology for Afforestation/Reforestation GHG Emissions Reduction and Sequestration
GS23253.description: The "Duguna Fango and Damot Weyde Assisted Farmer Managed Natural Regeneration for Sustainable Land Management and Livelihood Improvement Project" aims to regenerate and reforest degraded land in the Duguna Fango and Damot Weyde Woredas of South Ethiopia Regional State of Ethiopia. The area has undergone extensive environmental degradation in the past few decades due to overgrazing, farmland and settlement expansion, timber logging, firewood collection, charcoal production, and forest fire. The project will apply the assisted 'Farmer Managed Natural Regeneration (FMNR)' technique to reforest degraded lands in the target areas. FMNR is a low-cost, sustainable, and simple practice that communities can use to restore their land, increase its productivity, and build resilience within the community. FMNR is the systematic re-growth and management of trees from felled stumps, sprouting root systems or seeds remaining in the soils from cleared forests, or in woody thickets. FMNR is an empowering form of social forestry which gives individuals and communities both responsibility for care and nurture of naturally occurring woody vegetation and rewards from sustainable harvesting of wood and NTFP. A FMNR project ideally involves the entire community or landscape and is a practice that contributes to a range of desired development outcomes such as land restoration, sustainable agricultural production systems, livelihood and community development and climate mitigation and adaptation.

GS23254.description:
Brújula Verde is a large-scale, 30,000-hectare reforestation and ecosystem restoration project in Vichada, Colombia, designed to deliver high-integrity nature-based carbon removals while supporting biodiversity and community development. The project focuses on establishing diverse, mixed-species forests through the planting of both fast-growing pioneer species and a wide range of native trees, 
ultimately transitioning toward predominantly native forest cover. This approach enhances soil recovery, 
improves water and nutrient cycles, and builds long-term landscape resilience. By combining phased 
planting and enrichment strategies, Brújula Verde strengthens ecosystem services, contributes to 
Colombia's climate mitigation goals, and generates local employment and sustainable livelihood 
opportunities

GS23255.description: The Programme of Activity includes the sale, distribution and utilization of high-efficiency biomass burning technologies such as improved cookstoves and dryers in Vietnam. The conversion from traditional devices to improved cookstoves and dryers offers multiple benefits including: reducing biomass consumption, saving costs, reducing greenhouse gas emissions, contributing to environmental protection and aligning with sustainable development goals.

GS23256.description: The Project includes the sale, distribution and utilization of high-efficiency dryers in Thai Nguyen, Viet Nam to promote the sustainable green tea processing. The conversion from traditional devices to improved cookstoves and dryers offers multiple benefits including: reducing biomass consumption, saving costs, reducing greenhouse gas emissions, contributing to environmental protection and aligning with sustainable development goals.

GS23257.description: The purpose of the proposed mitigation activity is to provide residential users (HH) with energy-efficient cooking technology i.e., tier 5 Improved Charcoal Stoves (ICS) and safe water drinking systems that reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from the combustion of non-renewable woody biomass-based charcoal for cooking or boiling of water in Ghana. It also seeks to address water contamination issues, that heavily impact households, by providing a safe water source. Depending on the criticality of needs within the household, they will either be targeted with ICS or safe water drinking systems. The project will also provide financial savings for the HH, because of a reduction in charcoal consumption and will improve their health by reducing the exposure to indoor air pollution (IAP).

GS23258.description:
The purpose of the PoA, "Safe Water Programme in East Africa - Uganda", is to reduce greenhouse gas emissions due to the practice of burning non-renewable biomass, such as firewood and charcoal, for water treatment (e.g., boiling). This will be achieved by implementing community-based safe drinking water treatment and supply technologies while promoting renewable energy solutions (water treatment and supply is done by solar power) in the host country, the Republic of Uganda. The PoA will help improve access to clean water in rural and urban areas. 
WMVI is the CME of this programme and will implement the project activity through the Water Mission. This Christian engineering non-profit builds safe water, sanitation, and hygiene solutions in developing countries and disaster areas. As well as potentially implementing through other implementation partners in Uganda.  Water Mission Verified Impact (WMVI) is the Coordinating and Managing Entity (CME) of the PoA with the carbon Management partnership of PersistentClimate India Pvt Limited. To ensure access to the maximum number of communities, the programme will be implemented in collaboration with several partners, such as micro-entrepreneurs, NGOs, financial institutions, and local distribution partners.

GS23259.description: The purpose of the VPA, "VPA 1 Safe Water Programme in Uganda", is to reduce greenhouse gas emissions due to the practice of burning non-renewable biomass, such as firewood and charcoal, for water treatment (e.g., boiling). This will be achieved by implementing community-based safe drinking water treatment and supply technologies while promoting renewable energy solutions (water treatment and supply is done by solar power) in the host country, the Republic of Uganda. The PoA will help improve access to clean water in rural and urban areas. WMVI is the CME of this programme and will implement the project activity through the Water Mission. This Christian engineering non-profit builds safe water, sanitation, and hygiene solutions in developing countries and disaster areas. As well as potentially implementing through other implementation partners in Uganda. Water Mission Verified Impact (WMVI) is the Coordinating and Managing Entity (CME) of the PoA with the carbon Management partnership of PersistentClimate India Pvt Limited. To ensure access to the maximum number of communities, the programme will be implemented in collaboration with several partners, such as micro-entrepreneurs, NGOs, financial institutions, and local distribution partners.

GS23260.developer: Fair Climate Fund India Private Limited
GS23260.description:
The "Agroforestry Carbon Program for Resilient Himalayan Communities" aims to
restore approximately 6,430 hectares of long-abandoned agricultural land in Nepal's
mid-hill and Terai regions through the introduction of agroforestry species and the
promotion of sustainable practices like intercropping. The project will be carried out
in areas where much of the land has remained uncultivated for years and is owned
by small to medium-scale farmers. The key objectives of the project includes:
• Promotion of sustainable agroforestry practices that contribute to restoration of
agricultural land and improved productivity.
• The introduction of high-value tree species and linking farmers to market-oriented
agroforestry products, with an aim to improve their livelihoods and create long-term
income opportunities with plantation and other project activites.
• The project also aims to increase their capacity through training programs,
community mobilization, and knowledge-sharing, ensuring the local communities
with the skills and knowledge needed for sustainable land management.

GS23261.description:
The TASAR Project is an afforestation initiative designed to restore degraded and barren lands through the establishment of diverse forest tree plantations on privately owned lands belonging to marginalized communities as recognized in the Indian Constitution. Over a five-year period (2023–2027), the project aims to cover 15,200 hectares of fallow or degraded land, positively impacting approximately 14,000 farmers across 600 villages.
This initiative promotes the planting of indigenous host tree species for the Tasar silkworm (Antheraea mylitta Drury). The tree species planted will enhance biodiversity by improving habitat quality, stabilizing soil, and supporting pollinators and wildlife. Their diverse canopy and flowering cycles further support ecosystem resilience. Terminalia arjuna and Terminalia tomentosa serve as primary host species for the Tasar silkworm. These native trees, known for their longevity exceeding 50 years, thrive in depleted soils and effectively support Tasar silkworm rearing. Their robust growth also contributes to large-scale atmospheric CO₂ sequestration, enhancing climate change mitigation efforts. The initiative is expected to create a sustainable source of income for the participating farmers as the host trees support Tasar silkworm rearing, offering farmers a reliable source of income through the sale of silk cocoons, moth eggs known as seeds, and Tasar silk.

GS23264.description: The project includes the construction and operation of metal and mineral recovery plants in Switzerland. Each plant has the capacity to process thousands of tons of incinerator bottom ash (IBA) from nearby incinerators on an annual basis. Around half of materials from the incinerator waste are set to be recovered, among which is a significant share of valuable metals and mineral fractions. The recovered metal and mineral fractions are sold downstream and therefore re-enter the economic cycle. The activity results in the reduction of emissions through the replacement of virgin materials in manufacturing, avoiding emissions involved in the extraction and processing of such materials.

GS23265.description:
Multiple water supply systems, originally designed to serve a combined population of approximately 45,000 people across 12 villages in Ghana's Eastern and Ashanti regions, have fallen into a state of disrepair due to prolonged lack of maintenance and weak operational management. As a result, the systems are now considered practically inoperable, with significantly reduced functionality.
The infrastructure includes boreholes with submersible pumps, elevated water storage tanks, interconnected distribution pipelines and communal tap stations. These systems were initially developed through a private sector initiative and later transferred to the Ghana Red Cross Society. However, the receiving entity faced ongoing challenges related to limited technical capacity and financial constraints, which hindered the systems' maintenance and long-term performance.

GS23266.developer: Beijing MD Energy Technology Co. Ltd.
GS23266.description:
The Project comprises the application of one or more energy efficiency measures 
as retrofits to existing ships. The types of eligible retrofit measures include Design related measures、Propulsion measures、Machinery measures、Operating measures etc. These measures would reduce fossil fuel consumption and thereby reduce CO2 emissions. 
Since the ship in this project travels in international waters, shipping emissions and emissions reduction are not included in the GHG inventory of any country usually. The International Maritime Organisation (IMO, belonging to the UN) is responsible for setting commitments on emissions from ships, there is no Host Country for these 
projects. 
Moreover, there is no physical geographical location of the project activity. However, the ship has a unique identification number established by the IMO. As stated in Section "Baseline Methodology: Project Boundary" of the methodology "Retrofit Energy Efficiency Measures in Shipping": "The spatial project boundary is the geographical location of project ships in which vessels are clearly identified by their unique IMO-Number." 
.The proposed project is considered to be micro scale, since the expected emissions reductions are below 10,000 tCO2eq/year.

GS23270.description: This project aims to reduce the reliance on non-renewable biomass for cooking by introducing efficient, clean cooking technologies across Nigeria. This goal will be achieved through the distribution and installation of the EcoHome stoves.

GS23271.description: The project includes the construction and operation of a metal and mineral recovery plant in Switzerland. The plant has the capacity to process thousands of tons of incinerator bottom ash (IBA) from nearby incinerators on an annual basis. Around half of materials from the incinerator waste are set to be recovered, among which is a significant share of valuable metals and mineral fractions. The recovered metal and mineral fractions are sold downstream and therefore re-enter the economic cycle. The activity results in the reduction of emissions through the replacement of virgin materials in manufacturing, avoiding emissions involved in the extraction and processing of such materials.

GS23272.description: Mutina Power is developing the programme "Clean Cookstoves and Biofuel Solutions in Tanzania" (the PoA) in Tanzania. The programme activities aim to distribute highly-efficient cookstoves and sustainable biofuel to urban and peri-urban households and institutions in Northern and coastal areas of Tanzania. The main target group will be households using the three stone fire and other traditional and unsustainable cooking methods.

GS23273.description: Mutina Power will distribute and install 10,000 high efficiency Mimi Moto cooking stoves and locally produced biomass pellets to urban and peri-urban households in the coastal areas of Tanzania (Pwani Region, including Mafia Island). The project plans to distribute cookstoves to a mixture of urban and peri-urban target groups. The main focus group will be households using the three-stone fire and firewood as fuel for cooking. Commercial activities and public institutions might be included at further stages of the project implementation.

GS23274.description:
World Vision Australia intends to implement this Programme of Activities (PoA) for afforestation and reforestation activities in several states of Ethiopia. 

The PoA aims to regenerate degraded land through the implementation of the Farmer Managed Natural Regeneration (FMNR) practice and enrichment planting (described in the section A.3). By sequestering carbon, the PoA contributes to climate change mitigation efforts while improving local biodiversity, soil fertility, and water retention. These interventions aim to provide long-term benefits to local communities by creating sustainable livelihoods and promoting ecosystem services.

GS23275.description:
The "Nature-based Solutions for Regenerated Forests and Community Resilience in Chifra – Afar Region" aims to regenerate and reforest an area of approximately 4,756 ha in the Chifra Woredas of Afar Regional State of Ethiopia. This project will be developed as a Voluntary Project Activity (VPA) under the Gold Standard Programme of Activities (PoA): "Nature-based Solutions for Regenerated Forests and Community Resilience in Ethiopia". 

The project aims to restore the degraded rangelands in the Chifra Woreda by utilising Farmer-Managed Natural Regeneration (FMNR) as a primary approach, with the inclusion of enrichment planting, involving cultivating seedlings in nurseries.

GS23277.description:
Azimayi Improved Cookstoves in the Republic of Malawi" is a large-scale project that aims to distribute energy-efficient improved cooking solutions (ICS) in domestic households and communities in the Republic of Malawi (project location), thereby replacing traditional inefficient cooking devices that utilize firewood as a primary cooking fuel in the baseline. 

Traditional cooking methods (use of inefficient, solid biomass cooking devices like 3-stone fires/ open fires and/or traditional solid fuel stoves) prevalent across the Republic of Malawi generate significant volumes of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions attributed to the inefficient combustion of unsustainably sourced, non-renewable biomass (NRB) fuel.

The project activity includes the dissemination of project ICS to beneficiaries using traditional modes of cooking in the baseline. The project ICS employs natural draft technology to improve fuel combustion, aiding better heat transfer to the cooking pots.

GS23278.description:
The United States is home to over 700 million acres of forestland, nearly 7.5% of the world's forests, that provide clean water, recreation, and other life-sustaining resources to Americans. The importance of American forests to the global ecosystem and climate is central to the work of CC Project SPV, LLC ("Project Developer"), a US-based company that seeks to restore and conserve functional forestland throughout the United States for the primary purpose of increasing carbon sequestration. 

Using the Gold Standard Land Use and Forest Activities Requirements and A/R (afforestation and reforestation) methodologies, the Project Developer is implementing an afforestation project called the Chestnut Sustainable Restoration Megaton Project on multiple parcels of land within the United States. The Project Developer will be acquiring and leasing unproductive, intensively managed pasture and croplands to plant trees and restore diverse, native forests. The purpose of the project is to increase carbon stocks and sequester greenhouse gases while creating sustainably managed native forestland throughout the country. The Project Developer has extensive expertise in carbon project development and forest management. The Project Developer's employees will manage planted forests and maintain the project's Forest Stewardship Council certification.

GS23279.description: The VPA aims to provide end-users with affordable and highly adaptable clean cooking solutions. This initiative targets reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from the burning of non-renewable woody biomass for household cooking and heating. Additionally, the project envisions benefiting household members, particularly women, by lowering exposure to indoor air pollution, reducing healthcare expenses, and alleviating the drudgery of firewood collection, purchase, and use. Developed under the Gold Standard, this project ensures high social impact on the community, leading to large-scale local socio-economic benefits while achieving verifiable emission reductions.

GS23280.description:
The RANOVOLA project, building on infrastructure put in place by other HELVETAS initiatives, aims to ensure safe and sustainable access to clean water for the most vulnerable rural communities in Madagascar. 
The RANOVOLA project main objectives are to provide reliable access to clean water, improve public health by reducing the prevalence of waterborne diseases, strengthen the autonomy of local communities by collaborating with private operators to manage the operation and maintenance of the established infrastructure, support the ecological transition by limiting dependence on fossil fuels and firewood for water purification, and contribute to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by acting on health, environmental, economic, and social fronts. 
The RANOVOLA project infrastructure will rely on two main technologies: 1) gravitational systems, using water sources located at higher altitudes to transport water to communities without the need for additional energy; and 2) solar pumping systems, utilizing boreholes to ensure a constant and economical water supply. 
In both cases, water treatment is carried out by filtration, chlorination, and iron removal. The operation and management of the infrastructure will be ensured by private operators, under a decentralized management model in compliance with Malagasy legal frameworks.

GS23281.description: The RANOVOLA project, building on infrastructure put in place by other HELVETAS initiatives, aims to ensure safe and sustainable access to clean water for the most vulnerable rural communities in Madagascar. The RANOVOLA project main objectives are to provide reliable access to clean water, improve public health by reducing the prevalence of waterborne diseases, strengthen the autonomy of local communities by collaborating with private operators to manage the operation and maintenance of the established infrastructure, support the ecological transition by limiting dependence on fossil fuels and firewood for water purification, and contribute to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by acting on health, environmental, economic, and social fronts. The RANOVOLA project infrastructure will rely on two main technologies: 1) gravitational systems, using water sources located at higher altitudes to transport water to communities without the need for additional energy; and 2) solar pumping systems, utilizing boreholes to ensure a constant and economical water supply. In both cases, water treatment is carried out by filtration, chlorination, and iron removal. The operation and management of the infrastructure will be ensured by private operators, under a decentralized management model in compliance with Malagasy legal frameworks.

GS23282.description: The Sarkylmas Kuat Wind Power Project is a greenfield Independent Power Project located in the Mangystau Region of Kazakhstan. The Project involves the construction and operation of a 50 MW wind farm to provide renewable energy to Kazakhstan's national electricity grid(KEGOC).

GS23286.description: The project involves the deployment of a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) to store electricity generated from renewable energy sources such as solar or wind. The BESS enables time-shifting of renewable energy by storing surplus electricity during periods of low demand and discharging it during peak demand periods or grid stress events. This reduces the need for fossil fuel-based peaking power plants and supports grid stability and renewable energy integration. The system comprises battery, power conversion systems (inverters), battery management systems, and control software to optimize charging/discharging cycles. The project contributes to greenhouse gas (GHG) emission reductions by displacing grid electricity that would otherwise be generated from fossil fuels.

GS23290.description: Promoting Regenerative Agriculture for Nature (PRAN)" is a Programme of Activities (PoA) to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from rice farming based on traditional practices like continuous flooding in India. The PoA will implement improved water management techniques, such as intermittent flooding, alternate wetting and drying (AWD), direct seeded rice (DSR) and regenerative farming practices etc. in rice paddies across India.  The PoA applies the Gold Standard Methodology for methane emission Reduction by adjusted water management practice in rice cultivation, version 1.0.

GS23291.description: The proposed Voluntary Project Activity (VPA) is developed by Grow Indigo Private Limited and is implemented across states of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh in India. VPA implements improved water management techniques, such as intermittent flooding, alternate wetting and drying (AWD), direct seeded rice (DSR) and regenerative farming practices, etc. in rice paddies. This initiative aims to introduce and promote improved agricultural techniques specifically for rice farming, falling under the Land Use & Forestry (LUF) and Agriculture (AGR) categories.

GS23292.description:
The Restore Africa: Restoring Landscapes and Livelihoods in Western Uganda project is implemented in degraded agricultural landscapes in the Western (Afromontane) highlands and pastoral rangelands of mid-Western Uganda. Over several decades, these regions have experienced substantial deforestation and degradation, poor agriculture practices, overgrazing, and an unsustainable demand for fuelwood. Climate change, population increases, poverty and lack of economic opportunities further exacerbate pressure on the land. 
The project focuses on establishment of new trees (e.g. through manual planting and broadcast seeding) as well as the improved management activities that enhance the natural regeneration of established root stock (e.g. through coppice management) in 24 districts in Western Uganda involving more than 200,000 small farmer households. The aim is to both sequester carbon as well as generate a broad set of environmental and socio-economic co-benefits through the implementation of sustainable agroforestry practices at a landscape scale. Co-benefits, based on the restoration of ecosystem functions, include sustainable food production, enhanced local livelihoods, increased gender equality and the improvement of ecosystem services.
The project will collaborate and align with the many organizations already established in the area to enhance long-term sustainability and ensure that implementation occurs in an efficient, locally appropriate, and acceptable manner.

GS23293.description:
The Restore Africa: Restoring Landscapes and Livelihoods in Malawi project is implemented in degraded agricultural landscapes in the in the Northern, Central and Southern Regions of the country. Over 90% of households in the country depend on natural resources and subsistence agriculture to meet their livelihoods, food and energy needs. Extensive clearing of forest and woodlands for fuelwood, followed by conversion to cropland, is driving a high annual deforestation rate of 1%.
The project focuses on establishment of new trees (e.g. through manual planting and broadcast seeding) as well as the improved management activities that enhance the natural regeneration of established root stock (e.g. through coppice management) in seven districts in Malawi involving more than 150,000 small farmer households. The aim is to both sequester carbon as well as generate a broad set of environmental and socio-economic co-benefits through the implementation of sustainable agroforestry practices at a landscape scale. Co-benefits, based on the restoration of ecosystem functions, include sustainable food production, enhanced local livelihoods, increased gender equality and the improvement of ecosystem services.
The project will collaborate and align with the many organizations already established in the area to enhance long-term sustainability and ensure that implementation occurs in an efficient, locally appropriate, and acceptable manner.

GS23294.description:
The Restore Africa: Restoring Landscapes and Livelihoods in Coastal Kenya project is implemented in Kenya's coastal region, specifically in the Kwale and Kilifi counties. With an annual deforestation rate of 0.58%, Kenya faces significant forest loss, primarily driven by dependence on natural resources and extensive land degradation.  The primary causes of land degradation include unsustainable wood resource exploitation, the expansion of unsustainable cultivation practices, the spread of invasive species, pollution, and climate change.
The project focuses on establishment of new trees (e.g. through manual planting and broadcast seeding) as well as the improved management activities that enhance the natural regeneration of established root stock (e.g. through coppice management) in the Kwale and Kilifi counties in Kenya, involving more than 100,000 small farmer households. The aim is to both sequester carbon as well as generate a broad set of environmental and socio-economic co-benefits through the implementation of sustainable agroforestry practices at a landscape scale. Co-benefits, based on the restoration of ecosystem functions, include increased household income, enhanced local livelihoods, increased gender equality and the improvement of ecosystem services.
The project builds on extensive experience in socio-economic development within the region.

GS23295.description:
The Restore Africa: Restoring Landscapes and Livelihoods in Western Kenya and Rift Valley Kenya project is implemented in Kenya's Elgeyo-Marakwet, Migori and Narok counties. Over several decades, these counties have experienced substantial deforestation and degradation because of poor agricultural practices, overgrazing and unsustainable demand for fuelwood. The scenario - the continued degradation of land and erosion of livelihood opportunities – will most likely continue to occur unless there is a substantial and additional intervention
The project focuses on establishment of new trees (e.g. through manual planting and broadcast seeding) as well as the improved management activities that enhance the natural regeneration of established root stock (e.g. through coppice management) in the Elgeyo-Marakwet, Migori and Narok counties in Kenya, involving more than 75,000 small farmer households. The aim is to both sequester carbon as well as generate a broad set of environmental and socio-economic co-benefits through the implementation of sustainable agroforestry practices at a landscape scale. Co-benefits, based on the restoration of ecosystem functions, include increased household income, enhanced local livelihoods, increased gender equality and the improvement of ecosystem services.

GS23296.description:
The regular case voluntary project activity (VPA) is providing household water filtration units for marginalized households in India living in rural, urban, semi-urban areas. The VPA is a part of POA and its real case VPA, which will contribute to the reduction of greenhouse gases and socio-economic progress for communities who are relying on unsafe drinking water sources and thus the objective of the VPA is to disseminate household water treatment units in Madhya Pradesh, India so that the rural communities living in remote hilly areas have increased access of safe drinking water for their daily use and thus increased living standard for the poor and marginalized people. 
The regular case VPA under the GS Programme of Activity provides safe household drinking water treatment solutions to marginalized households at free of cost and replace the usage of equivalent quantity of fuel wood in traditional three stone fire or any other conventional wood stoves which are inefficient and smoke-intensive and which would have been used to boil the water to make it safe for drinking purposes.

GS23297.description: The project aims to bring a positive impact in the livelihoods of project beneficiaries by disseminating improved cooking devices in Nepal. The project ICSs will replace traditional/inefficient biomass stoves currently used as baseline technologies. The prevalent use of such traditional cooking systems in Nepal results in significant greenhouse gas emissions from the use of non-renewable biomass (NRB), which is often sourced unsustainably. Additionally, traditional biomass-based cooking generates high levels of smoke and particulate matter (PM), exposing the primary cook—usually women—to hazardous indoor air pollution (IAP). The improved cookstoves (ICSs) introduced by the project are designed to be thermally more efficient, reducing fuel consumption, cooking time, and emissions. As a result, the project contributes to GHG emission reductions while also creating a cleaner cooking environment and reducing IAP exposure for women and children.

GS23300.developer: Climate Balanced İklim Enerji Ticaret ve Eğitim Limited Şirketi
GS23300.description:
The "Idea Balance Safe Water Access Project" will be implemented on Zanzibar Island, part of the United Republic of Tanzania. The project focuses on rehabilitating non-functional boreholes that have not received maintenance from the government or any authorized entity. These efforts will be financed and coordinated by the IDEA Universal International Development and Environment Association (IDEA Universal), leveraging their extensive expertise in sustainable water access initiatives.

This initiative aims to restore orphaned boreholes, identified based on household need and proximity to communities without alternative drinking water sources within a 1 km radius. By providing access to safe and clean drinking water, the project intends to reduce greenhouse gas emissions associated with boiling unsafe water and to decrease reliance on non-renewable biomass, mitigating environmental degradation and promoting sustainable resource use.

GS23301.description:
The purpose of the VPA is to disseminate Safe Water Supply (SWS) devices such as Institutional water treatment (IWT) and Household Water Treatment (HWT) technologies and Improved cookstoves in households and communities of Rwanda, Africa. The filters and/or Improved cookstoves are distributed to households/institutions which were earlier using wood and/or charcoal on rudimentary stoves for cooking/boiling or were consuming untreated water, for households where filters are distributed. The project makes the end-users energy efficient and reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions otherwise resulting from the burning of non-renewable woody biomass and/or charcoal in baseline scenario. 
The project boundary is the geographical boundary of Rwanda, Africa where the water filters/Improved cookstoves are proposed to be distributed.

GS23302.description:
The purpose of this Real VPA is to reduce greenhouse gas emissions in industry in Kenya by reducing the use of energy from heavy fuel oil in the baseline by substituting it with renewable biomass briquettes, made from bagasse which is a waste stream from the sugar industry. Sugar is an annual crop and therefore renewable . The fuel oil in the baseline is deemed "non-renewable". The main greenhouse gas being reduced by the project is carbon dioxide.  

More specifically, Tamuwa Limited (the Project Implementer) sells briquettes to Kensalt in 
Malindi that makes edible salt from sea water.

GS23303.description:
Infosys Limited the project developer along with implementation partners is implementing Agroforestry projects in India.
The project aims to enhance the livelihood of farmers and local communities. The primary aim of the project is to improve the social, economic and environmental conditions of the community along with estimating the carbon sequestration capacity thorough agroforestry in alignment with the SDG goals.

GS23304.developer: GREEN SPARK SOLUTIONS AUSTRALIA PTY LTD

GS23306.description: The purpose of the project is to generate electricity by harnessing the solar and wind energy by using solar photovoltaic & Wind turbine generator technologies and there by feed the generated electricity to the Indian national grid. Project involves the installation of 60 MW Solar Photovoltaic Power Plant & Wind power plant combined with BESS (60 MWh) in Uruchinthala, Tadipatri Tehsil, Dist. Anantapur, Andhra Pradesh. The project is yet to be commissioned and the generated electricity will be continuously supplied to the Indian grid. The power purchase agreement had been signed for the project on 31/07/2024 between SOLAR ENERGY CORPORATION OF INDIA LIMITED and CLEAN RENEWABLE ENERGY BARMER PRIVATE LIMITED. with rated capacity of renewable energy components as: Solar – 75 MWac; Wind Power – 79.2 MW; and ESS – 60/60 MW/60 MWh.

GS23307.description: The Programme of Activities (PoA) "TASC SOLUM - Sequestration and Optimised Landscapes Using Microbials" aims to improve the health of agricultural land in South Africa by using natural biostimulants to enhance soil carbon sequestration. The main goal of the project is to remove carbon dioxide (CO2) from the atmosphere and store it permanently in agricultural soils, which is good for the environment and can help reduce the effects of climate change by decreasing greenhouse gas emissions (GHG). Current intensive and high-input forms of agriculture are leading to biodiversity loss, soil erosion, poor water retention, decreased drought resilience, GHG emissions, decreased plant health and nutrition, and decreased soil health. Applying regenerative agricultural practices addresses these issues via several ways, including precision application of biological and chemical inputs, minimising soil disturbance, inter-cropping, cover cropping, and integrating livestock when possible. This project within the regenerative agriculture programme will focus on the precision application of biological and chemical inputs. More specifically, the application of biostimulants for soil revitalisation.

GS23308.description: The Programme of Activities (PoA) "TASC SOLUM - Sequestration and Optimised Landscapes Using Microbials" aims to improve the health of agricultural land in South Africa by using natural biostimulants to enhance soil carbon sequestration. TASC is including this Voluntary Project Activity within the PoA. The main goal of the project is to remove carbon dioxide (CO2) from the atmosphere and store it permanently in agricultural soils, which is good for the environment and can help reduce the effects of climate change by decreasing greenhouse gas emissions (GHG).Current intensive and high-input forms of agriculture are leading to biodiversity loss, soil erosion, poor water retention, decreased drought resilience, GHG emissions, decreased plant health and nutrition, and decreased soil health. Applying regenerative agricultural practices addresses these issues via several ways, including precision application of biological and chemical inputs, minimising soil disturbance, inter-cropping, cover cropping, and integrating livestock when possible. This project within the regenerative agriculture programme will focus on the precision application of biological and chemical inputs.

GS23309.description: Mozambique is classified as a Least Developed Country by the United Nations, and only half of Mozambicans have access to improved water supply in rural areas. Handpumps, which are commonly found in communities, often fall into disrepair shortly after installation due to insufficient maintenance, lack of access to spare parts, and financial support. The Pungue project, developed by Removall, aims to rehabilitate and sustain handpumps across Sofala province of Mozambique. It will avoid the consumption of firewood by households and lead to a reduction of carbon dioxide emissions.

GS23310.description: The VPA comprises the group of the independent activities that uses photovoltaic (PV) technology which enables to convert solar radiation into electrical energy. All activities included into the VPA envisage the installation of solar systems.

GS23314.description: The VPA comprises the group of the independent activities that uses photovoltaic (PV) technology which enables to convert solar radiation into electrical energy. All activities included into the VPA envisage the installation of solar systems.

GS23321.description:
The project will disseminate improved cook stoves (ICS) – to households within Tanzania. By providing clean cooking, the project will ensure that households consume less firewood during the process of cooking and as a result there shall be a reduction of carbon dioxide emissions from the combustion process. 
Most people in Sub-Saharan Africa rely on gathering biomass for cooking, in particular in rural areas, which dramatically damages health and impairs productivity improvements. The procurement and consumption of these fuels define the character of everyday life in many developing countries.
In line to its vision of delivering high impact related to health, savings and convenience, SDG 13 Ventures Pte. Ltd. is undertaking an extensive distribution programme to create a nation-wide access of Clean Cookstoves for low-income consumer.
The project will contribute in achieving SDGs including, SDG-01: 1 No poverty, SDG-3: Good Health and Well Being, SDG-5: Gender Equality, SDG 7- Affordable and Clean energy, SDG 8: Full and productive employment and decent work for all, SDG 10 Reduced Inequalities and SDG-13: Climate Action. The programme would result in GHG emission reductions and other impact outcomes which can be traded internationally and the revenue collected from such trade will benefit the scaling up of the project and thereby assist other households who are still using traditional stoves.

GS23322.developer: CHRISTIAN EAST AFRICA AND EQUATORIAL DEVELOPMENT (CEED) FOUNDATION LTD
GS23322.description: This project seeks to reduce carbon emissions by providing new clean water sources to rural villages in Uganda where the only means of access to clean water is to collect it from surface ponds and streams and boiling it for safe use. This real case is for a set of 10 villages in the Bunyoro-Kitara area of Western Uganda that will be provided with a new borehole for actual GHG emission reduction through the provision of clean water.

GS23325.description: Mozambique is classified as a Least Developed Country by the United Nations, and only half of Mozambicans have access to improved water supply in rural areas. Handpumps, which are commonly found in communities, often fall into disrepair shortly after installation due to insufficient maintenance, lack of access to spare parts, and financial support. The Pungue project, developed by Removall, aims to rehabilitate and sustain handpumps across Sofala province of Mozambique. It will avoid the consumption of firewood by households and lead to a reduction of carbon dioxide emissions.

GS23328.description: The ATEC Biodigesters in Bangladesh project is designed to serve rural households that primarily rely on fi rewood and biomass fuels for cooking. The primary target group consists of small-scale farming households that own 3 to 5 cows, as they can eff ectively utilize biogas technology to meet their cooking needs. This initiative aims to tackle the pressing challenges of clean cooking, environmental degradation, and rural household energy dependence by providing sustainable cooking solutions for low-income households. By introducing ATEC's biodigesters and biogas stoves, this project will replace traditional firewood stoves with highly efficient and eco-friendly alternatives. Beyond environmental benefits, the project is designed to improve the well-being of household members, particularly women, infants, and children. By reducing exposure to indoor air pollution, it helps lower the risk of respiratory illnesses and related health expenses. Additionally, it alleviates the burden of fi rewood collection, freeing up valuable time for education, economic activities, and improved quality of life.

GS23329.description:
The Sun Power Project is a 30 MW (AC) photovoltaic solar plant located in the municipality of Nagarote, within the department of León, Nicaragua. This facility will comprise 62,070 solar modules, achieving a total installed capacity of 38 MWp and a net capacity of 30 MW. 
The primary objective of this project is to contribute to the development of Nicaragua's electricity sector while adhering to sustainability principles and fostering the transformation of the country's energy matrix towards renewable and clean energy sources. The solar park aims to comply with international climate change mitigation standards, aligning with worldwide efforts to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and promote a more sustainable future.
In conclusion, the SunPower Project is not only designed to enhance Nicaragua's energy supply but also plays a pivotal role in supporting the country's commitments to environmental sustainability and facilitating the transition to a cleaner, more responsible energy matrix.

GS23330.developer: CICLUS AMBIENTAL DO BRASIL S A
GS23330.description:
1. Project Design and Scenarios
The project aims to collect and treat landfill gas (Landfill Gas – LFG) in various scenarios to reduce methane emissions. The planned scenarios include:
•Controlled flaring of collected gas;
•Supplying treated gas to industrial, commercial, or residential consumers;
•Using gas as fuel for electricity generation.
These scenarios will be applied according to the specific characteristics and needs of each landfill included in the program.
At the Santa Rosa Waste Treatment Center (CTR) in Seropédica (Rio de Janeiro – Brazil), the current scenario involves the capture of landfill gas (LFG) for combustion and distribution to external consumers. In the future, infrastructure is planned for electricity generation from the collected gas.
2. Technologies and Measures
The project uses modern technologies for LFG capture, treatment, and utilization, such as:
•Vertical and horizontal wells for gas collection;
•High-efficiency flaring systems;
•Infrastructure for gas treatment, including contaminant removal;
•Infrastructure for transporting biogas by trucks for external thermal applications.
For future phases, CTR Santa Rosa also plans to install modular equipment for electricity generation.
Additionally, the project includes strict monitoring to ensure operational efficiency and safety.
3. Geographic Boundaries
Currently, the project only includes CTR Santa Rosa in Seropédica/RJ. Geographic coordinates: -22.795703 (latitude) and -43.760558 (longitude).

GS23331.description: The Indonesia Sustainable Ride Program by EcoSecurities (PoA) aims to distribute electric or hybrid vehicles in Indonesia. The distribution and usage of electric or hybrid vehicles will reduce the consumption of gasoline and other fossil fuel from the use of regular fuel-combustion engine vehicles.  This reduced consumption will reduce the amount of greenhouse gas emission resulting from the vehicles usage.

GS23332.description: The Sustainable Electric Motorbike Ride Project by ESB and EcoSecurities (VPA) aims to promote the adoption of electric motorbikes by making them more accessible through the sales or rental of up to 501,000 electrics motor bikes or scooters over 5 to 6 year time in Indonesia as part of the PoA.  The use of electric motor bikes and scooters to replace conventional fuel-powered motorbikes will reduce the consumption of gasoline and other fossil fuels consumed in regular fuel-combustion motorcycle. With the reduced consumption, the amount of greenhouse gas emission resulting from the motorcycle usage will also decrease, contributing to a more sustainable transportation system.

GS23333.description:
Erguvan Enerji Elektrik Üretim A.Ş. plans to launch the Göktepe Wind Power Plant Capacity Increase Project with a total installed capacity of 105.64 MWm / 105.64 MWe, based on the Electricity Generation License obtained from the Energy Market Regulatory Authority on 04/06/2020. The project will be implemented within the borders of Esenköy in Çınarcık District, and Mecidiye Village and Karşıyaka in Armutlu District, Yalova Province.
As part of the project, 19 wind turbines will be constructed and a Battery Energy Storage System will also be established. The electricity generated at the plant will be transmitted to the Yalova WPP and Yares Yalova WPP Transformer Substations via a 154 kV transmission line.
Scheduled to be commissioned in 2029, the Göktepe Wind Power Plant Capacity Increase Project is expected to supply approximately 260,625 MWh of electricity annually to the grid. Due to its renewable energy source, the wind power plant will also contribute to a reduction of approximately 165,366 tons of CO₂ equivalent emissions per year.

GS23334.description: This project aims to reduce the reliance on non-renewable biomass for cooking by introducing efficient, clean cooking technologies across Nigeria. This goal will be achieved through the distribution and installation of the EcoHome stoves.

GS23336.description: Installation of solar water supply systems with community tap stands and hand pumps across Plateau State, Northern Nigeria

GS23337.description: Voluntary Project Activity 2 (VPA-2) under the HECTOR project represents a transformative initiative aimed at rural villages in the Anantapur District of Andhra Pradesh. This project is specifically designed to tackle the critical issues surrounding the availability of safe drinking water, aligning with the broader goals of India's Jal Jivan Mission. VPA-2 focuses on revolutionizing water purification by introducing advanced technologies, including automated chlorination units, UV disinfection systems, and real-time water quality monitoring powered by IoT and AI-ML. The strategic implementation of these solutions seeks to address the persistent challenges in rural areas, significantly improving water quality standards and enhancing access to safe drinking water for the communities involved.

GS23338.description:
The "Resilient Futures" Programme of Activities (PoA) is a community-driven initiative designed to address the interlinked challenges of poverty, environmental degradation, and climate change across vulnerable rural regions. By deploying scalable, high-impact interventions—such as improved cookstoves, safe water technologies, biochar production, and regenerative agroforestry—this PoA aims to reduce and remove greenhouse gas emissions while strengthening the adaptive capacity of local communities.

Led by trusted local partners and supported by ethical climate finance, the PoA empowers women, improves health outcomes, restores ecosystems, and increases household income and food security. 

This programme contributes to multiple Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly SDG 1 (No Poverty), SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being), SDG 5 (Gender Equality), SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation), SDG 13 (Climate Action), and SDG 15 (Life on Land). 
The PoA is designed to enable the rapid scaling of ethical, verifiable carbon projects in West Africa and beyond—delivering measurable climate impact and real, lasting change for people and planet.

GS23339.description: The Empowering Communities Through Improved Cookstoves project in rural Togo distributes fuel-efficient improved cookstoves (ICS) to replace traditional, inefficient three-stone fires commonly used in rural households. The cookstoves are manufactured locally in Togo, supporting infrastructure development, generating employment, and stimulating economic growth in the region. By reducing the amount of firewood required for cooking, the project alleviates the time and physical burden of firewood collection—a task that disproportionately falls on women and girls. This, in turn, enables greater access to education and income-generating opportunities. In addition to reducing greenhouse gas emissions, the project delivers a range of co-benefits, including: Improved indoor air quality, reducing the incidence of respiratory and eye-related illnesses caused by smoke inhalation from traditional stoves. Reduced pressure on local forests through decreased firewood demand, slowing deforestation and preserving biodiversity. Lower household expenditure on cooking fuel due to more efficient wood use. Increased time savings for women and children, enabling greater focus on education, caregiving, and economic activities. Job creation and skill development through local cookstove production and distribution. By addressing both climate change and local development needs, the project contributes to eight Sustainable Development Goals.

GS23340.description: The Niger Delta Community-Driven Mangrove Restoration Project is a scalable initiative focused on restoring the historically mangrove-rich wetlands of the Niger Delta through a community-led approach. The Niger Delta—the largest river delta in Africa and home to the world's third-largest mangrove forest—has faced severe degradation over the past decades due to a variety of pressures. This has compromised biodiversity, diminished livelihoods, and increased vulnerability to flooding and erosion for the 30 million people who live there. This project aims to restore the ecosystem through training local communities to plant native, locally adapted mangrove species, while also addressing the causes of mangrove loss. Its objectives are to: • Empower communities by providing the livelihood support, education, and tools needed to become long-term ecosystem stewards and bolster their resilience in a climate-changing world, • Restore a critical ecosystem and its services while promoting biodiversity by rebuilding the habitats of numerous species, strengthening regional food security, and providing flood and storm protection. • And finally, sequester carbon in the fight against climate change while utilizing mangroves as a powerful nature-based solution. Rooted in strong local partnerships and ecosystem restoration approaches, the project is designed to scale and serve as a model for community-first restoration across Nigeria and the wider region.

GS23342.description: UpEnergy Group will work with micro-entrepreneurs, NGOs, financial institutions, local distribution partners etc. to provide residential/institutions users with clean cooking technologies. UpEnergy would ensure the last-mile distribution/installation of the energy efficient/clean energy technologies to the beneficiaries. This VPA is implemented in host country-Zambia.
