UpEnergy would ensure the last-mile distribution/installation of the energy efficient/clean energy technologies to the beneficiaries. This VPA is implemented in host country-Zambia.

GS23355.description:
The project aims to restore and maintain non-functional boreholes in rural, water-scarce regions of South Africa. By providing reliable access to clean groundwater, it reduces dependence on unsafe water sources and the need to boil water using traditional fuels. The initiative also builds local capacity by training and employing community technicians for ongoing maintenance, ensuring long-term sustainability and resilience. 

The project improves access to safe drinking water, leading to a reduction in waterborne diseases and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from the use of traditional fuels for water purification. It lessens the burden on women and children by minimizing the time spent collecting water, enhances community health and safety, creates local employment opportunities, and promotes awareness of safe water and hygiene practices.

GS23356.description:
The project aims to restore and maintain non-functional boreholes in rural, water-scarce regions of South Africa. By providing reliable access to clean groundwater, it reduces dependence on unsafe water sources and the need to boil water using traditional fuels. The initiative also builds local capacity by training and employing community technicians for ongoing maintenance, ensuring long-term sustainability and resilience.

The project improves access to safe drinking water, leading to a reduction in waterborne diseases and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from the use of traditional fuels for water purification. It lessens the burden on women and children by minimizing the time spent collecting water, enhances community health and safety, creates local employment opportunities, and promotes awareness of safe water and hygiene practices.

GS23357.description: The proposed project is a Voluntary Project Activity (VPA) focused on afforestation and will be implemented in Odisha, India. It aims to sequester atmospheric carbon dioxide through plantations. The project will promote native and climate-resilient species, with the special emphasis to support sustainable livelihoods through community participation and agroforestry practices. It will also enhance biodiversity and improve soil health. Furthermore, the project generates temporary employment for local communities during the implementation and management of the plantation. The project aligns with multiple SDGs, including climate action, life on land, and no poverty.

GS23358.description:
Project Saladillo transforms 15,946 hectares of cattle grazing land, subject to continual slash-and-burn practices, in Paraguay's Cordillera region into a mosaic plantation combining commercial and conservation forestry. It prioritises long-term ecological resilience and sustainable development. The project integrates 25% permanent conservation with 75% selectively harvested forestry, maintaining at least 96% continuous forest cover. This model prevents deforestation by producing sustainable timber and biomass, while enhancing biodiversity through protection of native forests and riparian corridors, supporting habitat continuity and safeguarding local fauna.
An estimated 1,122,437 tons of CO₂ will be sequestered over 50+ years. High-precision carbon monitoring uses LiDAR-based models calibrated with field sampling to ensure accuracy in both accessible and remote areas.
Saladillo generates formal, year-round employment through staggered planting and harvesting, eliminating informal labour, reducing seasonal risks, and ensuring steady income for local communities. It collaborates closely with local NGOs such as Fundación Moisés Bertoni and the University of Asunción, integrating community engagement, biodiversity monitoring, and academic research.
The project adheres to the highest environmental and social safeguards, aligning with FSC certification, IFC Performance Standards, and World Bank guidelines, contributing to SDGs 8, 12, 13, and 15.

GS23359.developer: Sow and Reap Agro Private Limited
GS23359.description:
The project aims to promote agroforestry practices by planting coconut trees (Cocos nucifera) on fallow farmland systems in the Indian state of Karnataka. This coconut plantation initiative falls under the Afforestation and Reforestation (A/R) project activity, focusing on implementing agroforestry practices to enhance the resilience, productivity,
and sustainability of farming systems by enhancing farmer income. 

The project developer Sow & Reap Agro Pvt. Ltd.  aims to achieve the goals of (a) enhancing farmer income through climate resilient systems, and (b) mitigate the impact of climate change by sequestering atmospheric CO2 into coconut tree biomass.

GS23360.description:
The Madad Electric Cookstove (MEC) Project is abased clean energy initiative developed by Third Pole Solutions in partnership with the Aga Khan Rural Support Programme (AKRSP) as the coordinating and implementing agency in Pakistan. The project aims to replace traditional wood-burning stoves—locally known as bukhari—and 3-stone cooking methods with energy-efficient electric cookstoves.

The Primary objectives of the Project is to reduce the use of wood for cooking, thereby reducing the GHG emissions and having a positive impact on the Climate (SDG 13). By adopting clean, sustainable cooking practices (SDG7), the Project will focus on ensuring healthy lives and promoting well-being for all by addressing the impact of environment factors on health (SDG3), reduce time spent on collecting or buying firewood resulting in cost savings and increasing the household's disposable income (SDG1) and promote gender equality by involving women's community groups (SDG5)

GS23361.description: In most of the countries on the African continent including Ghana, cooking is done on either 3-stone fires or very inefficient traditional cookstoves, consuming a lot of fuel, in particular non-renewable firewood and charcoal. The high biomass consumption has negative impacts on the environment leading to deforestation and land degradation, Greenhouse Gas Emissions (GHG) emissions, loss of soil fertility and soils' reduced ability of water retention. Further, indoor air pollution through health-damaging pollutants while combusting firewood and charcoal result in diseases like e.g. pneumonia, stroke, ischemic heart diseases, chronic obstructive pulmonary diseases and lung cancer. The purpose of a 'STERLING IMPROVED COOKSTOVES PROJECT Carbon Project Activities included under the Gold Standard', is to disseminate highly efficient improved cookstoves (ICS to urban, peri-urban and/or rural users (households, communities, institutions, or SMEs) in Ghana. Several greenhouse gases (GHG), including carbon dioxide, are produced as a result of the incomplete combustion of biomass as used in cook stoves. More GHG emissions result from the use of biomass which is non-renewable. ICS improves heat transfer efficiency as compared to the baseline traditional cook stoves, thereby reducing both the amount of woody biomass used by unit appliances implemented and the emission of GHGs.

GS23363.description:
The Ghana Cocoa Agroforestry Livelihoods Project is designed to enhance the productivity and long-term sustainability of cocoa farming systems while improving the livelihoods of the communities that depend on them. By introducing an agroforestry model that integrates shade tree species into existing cocoa plantations, the project aims to extend the productive lifespan of cocoa trees and strengthen the system's resilience to environmental challenges, including pests and diseases. This initiative will be carried out in close partnership with the local communities, with a focus on engaging youth teams to lead on the ground implementation. 
The project is expected to reach 11,000 farmers for an implementation area of 17,000 hectares. The project's main activity consists of planting shade and fruit trees within the existing cocoa plantations. Nine different native tree species will be incorporated into the farms to achieve a target density of 90 shade trees per hectare. 
Additionally, the new tree plantations will be associated with the training and coaching of the farmers in sustainable agroforestry practices such as tree management, pruning and Integrated Pest Management (IPM). The implementation of these practices is expected to increase the productive lifetime of the cocoa species and reduce the incidence of pests and diseases on the targeted trees. The project is expected to sequester 2.61 MtCO2e within 30 years.

GS23364.description:
The Madad Electric Cookstove (MEC) Project is abased clean energy initiative developed by Third Pole Solutions in partnership with the Aga Khan Rural Support Programme (AKRSP) as the coordinating and implementing agency in Pakistan. The project aims to replace traditional wood-burning stoves—locally known as bukhari—and 3-stone cooking methods with energy-efficient electric cookstoves.

The Primary objectives of the Project is to reduce the use of wood for cooking, thereby reducing the GHG emissions and having a positive impact on the Climate (SDG 13). By adopting clean, sustainable cooking practices (SDG7), the Project will focus on ensuring healthy lives and promoting well-being for all by addressing the impact of environment factors on health (SDG3), reduce time spent on collecting or buying firewood resulting in cost savings and increasing the household's disposable income (SDG1) and promote gender equality by involving women's community groups (SDG5)

GS23365.description: The Gold Standard for the Global Goals (GS4GG) Programme of Activities (PoA) "The Cameroon Clean Households´ Energy Program" (the CCHEP PoA) aims at the introduction and distribution of innovative clean energy solutions to households in Cameroon. The PoA serves as a framework under which different Voluntary Project Activities (subprojects or "VPAs") will be implemented.

GS23366.description: The Heat Retention Cooking VPA No. 1 aims at distributing around 15,000 to 20,000 heat retention cooking bags, so called "Wonderbags". These Wonderbags retain a large portion of cooking energy by storing dishes that are brought to the boiling point in a heat insulated bag, where the cooking process is finished without the need of further heating. Therefore, they greatly reduce the consumption of traditional cooking fuels, mainly fuelwood, charcoal and liquified petroleum gas (LPG).

GS23367.description: The Carbono Vivo Marañón Project is a long-term environmental and climate initiative that supports the transition to sustainable land use through the establishment of agroforestry systems based on cashew (Anacardium occidentale) in Colombia. Designed to generate social, environmental, and climate benefits, the PoA brings together producers, processors, marketers, and local communities across the value chain to promote rural development, biodiversity conservation, and carbon removal.

GS23368.description: Carbono Vivo Marañón KardiaNuts & Kashú is the first real-case VPA under the PoA, implemented in the department of Vichada, Colombia. It operationalizes the PoA framework by establishing the first set of agroforestry systems with cashew in collaboration with local stakeholders. The VPA focuses on generating measurable climate impact through carbon sequestration, while contributing to local livelihoods and sustainable land management.

GS23369.description: The purpose of the Improved Cooking Project in Madagascar is to mitigate climate change by reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions through the distribution of efficient cookstoves. This project aims to enhance environmental sustainability and improve the health and socio-economic conditions of rural and urban communities in Madagascar. By replacing traditional open-fire cooking methods with improved cookstoves, the project will significantly reduce fuel consumption, thereby decreasing deforestation rates and promoting the sustainable management of natural resources. The project aligns with the Gold Standard's objectives of delivering real, measurable, and long-term emission reductions and promoting sustainable development benefits.

GS23372.description:
The proposed project activity 'Accelerating Access to Clean Cooking in Kenya Project by Nyalore Impact Limited' will be implemented by Nyalore Impact Limited' with the purpose of promoting and distributing clean cooking devices that include Induction Cookers (ICs) and Electric Pressure Cookers (EPCs) to house-holds in Kenya. The project intends to accelerate access to clean cooking by displacing use of inefficient biomass cooking devices and polluting fuels. Use of the project technology will displace GHG emissions from the thermal energy consumption required for cooking by households. This will consequently contribute towards reduced household air pollution and support several sustainable development goals. The project's primary target is end-users who cook using inefficient biomass cookstoves and polluting fuels such as kerosene both in the urban and rural areas of Kenya.

Goals and Objectives of the Project Activity
According to the 2022 KNBS Demographic and Health Survey (DHS) report, 68.5% of Kenyan population still highly dependent on traditional cooking fuels, with firewood being the predominant cooking fuel. This presents a climate change challenge and has motivated the project developer to develop an innovative project that will accelerate the transition to cleaner cooking solutions to mitigate the negative impacts associated with the use of traditional fuels.

GS23373.description: Infosys Limited is spearheading a visionary large-scale agroforestry initiative under a proposed Programme of Activities (PoA), spanning diverse regions across India. This transformative project focuses on restoring degraded lands through the plantation of a wide variety of climate-resilient agroforestry species. At its heart lies the active participation of local farmers and communities-empowering them through sustainable land-use practices that not only regenerate ecosystems but also enhance livelihoods. By blending traditional knowledge with modern ecological approaches, the project is committed to building climate resilience, enriching biodiversity, and fostering long-term socio-economic growth for rural communities.

GS23374.description:
The proposed initiative is a Voluntary Project Activity (VPA) focused on agroforestry plantations, to be implemented in Odisha, India. Implemented by the SGI Foundation, the project aims to sequester atmospheric carbon dioxide through large-scale plantation activities, while simultaneously enhancing local biodiversity, improving soil health, and promoting sustainable livelihoods. The project emphasizes the cultivation of native and climate-resilient agroforestry species such as Mango, Teak, Cashew, Jackfruit, Guava, and other regionally suitable trees under the first VPA. Active participation from local farmers is central to the initiative, empowering them to adopt agroforestry practices that improve income security and resilience to climate variability.
Beyond its environmental benefits, the project contributes significantly to socio-economic development by generating temporary employment for community members during the plantation's establishment and maintenance phases. It also strengthens long-term sustainability through capacity-building and inclusive community engagement. The initiative supports multiple SDGs, including Climate Action (SDG 13), Life on Land (SDG 15), and No Poverty (SDG 1), by integrating carbon sequestration with biodiversity conservation and rural development. A core objective of the project is to quantify the carbon sequestration potential of agroforestry plantations in Odisha while uplifting farming communities through sustainable land-use practices.

GS23375.description: ATH Bioenergy is promoting the implementation of four organic waste recovery plants in the Canary Islands with the aim of transforming the waste generated in the hotel, commercial and agri-food sectors into biomethane and high-quality organic fertilisers with the use of CO2. This initiative represents a firm step towards the energy transition, the decarbonization of the territory, the promotion of a real circular economy in the archipelago, and the contribution to the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals to which the Company is committed, positively impacting the local community.

GS23376.description:
The plant, located in the municipality of Agüimes, in Gran Canaria, is expected to come into operation in October 2025, at which time a three-month operational test phase will be carried out to guarantee the efficiency and safety of the process. The implementation to obtain emission reductions is estimated in the first quarter of 2026.
This first plant will be located next to the Southeast treatment plant, in the port free zone of Gran Canaria, which will facilitate its logistical integration and connectivity with distribution channels. It will be designed to manage up to 31,000 tonnes of organic waste per year, from which approximately 2,242 tonnes of biomethane per year will be produced, equivalent to 31,141 MWh of energy. This production of this energy vector represents a sustainable alternative to about 2,832 tons of propane gas, which will allow a significant reduction in the use of fossil fuels and polluting gas emissions and contribute to local climate and energy governance. 
As for the size and scope of the activity of the facility, it is estimated that it can serve some 45-65 hotels since the capacity of the digester, is 31,000 t/y of organic waste.
Among the key components of the project, the production of biomethane as a renewable substitute for propane gas and diesel stands out.

GS23378.description: The Biomass Gasification VPA No. 1 aims at distributing biomass gasification cookstoves. These stoves, that allow for clean cooking with pellets and other biomass, will replace traditional cooking, mainly fuelwood and charcoal responsible for deforestation and indoor air pollution in Cameroon.

GS23379.developer: University of Guam Center for Island Sustainability & Sea Grant (UOG CIS & SG)
GS23379.description:
The Ugum Watershed Reforestation and Carbon Offset Initiative targets 100 acres (~40.5 hectares) of degraded, non-forested savanna land in Southern Guam, within the villages of Inalåhan and Talo'fo'fo'. While the site has been undergoing restoration since 2019 under the Guam Restoration of Watersheds (GROW) initiative, only plantings occurring after April 7, 2023 are eligible for carbon crediting under this project. 
The site plays a critical ecological role: it feeds into the Ugum River, which is essential for the southern municipal water supply. Restoration activities reduce erosion, improve water quality, and enhance forest cover to buffer against the region's susceptibility to fire, storm events, and flash flooding.

GS23380.description:
The main purpose of the project activity is the distribution of fuel-efficient improved
cook stoves (ICS) specifically in the states of Nigeria. The Improved cook-stoves distributed through this project has replaced the low-efficient traditional cook-stoves. Through this project, the distribution and installation of high thermal efficient improved cook stoves (ICS) has been undertaken for households. The ICS burns non-renewable woody biomass and/or charcoal more efficiently thereby improving thermal energy transfer to pots, hence saving fuel wood and greenhouse gases. Not only will this halt the rapidly progressing deforestation but will also reduce health hazards from indoor air (smoke) pollution and women and children will have to spend less time collecting firewood.

GS23381.description: This project introduces the Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) method in rice cultivation across the different districts of Eastern region of India. By adopting this water-saving irrigation technique, the project aims to significantly reduce methane emissions and optimize water usage, contributing to climate change mitigation and resource conservation. Beyond environmental benefits, the initiative seeks to empower local farmers through targeted training and capacity-building programs. The project also delivers tangible socio-economic co-benefits to farming communities, such as improved resilience, knowledge transfer, and potential income enhancement, thereby supporting sustainable rural development in the region.

GS23383.description:
This PoA aims to save water and reduce methane emissions during rice farming by introducing water management technology to rice farming, which is one of the main greenhouse gas emission sources in Cambodia.  By participating in this project, farmers can produce low-carbon rice without reducing rice productivity and participate in mitigating climate change.  ThanksCarbon, a business developer, has introduced an AI-based satellite technology into this project to reduce the burden on individual farmers for data collection and improve the convenience of monitoring data collection and MRV transparency.

Farmers will be motivated and trained to refrain from continuously flooding their fields by putting the suggested AWD technology into effect, which would cut down on the quantity of CH4 emissions that would have been produced in the baseline situation. The sole change made to the project scenario is the adoption of alternating wetting and drying conditions rather than the submerged condition. Other than that, the project keeps the current agricultural techniques in place and does not introduce any new activities that might increase greenhouse gas emissions.

GS23387.description: Delivering Safe Drinking Water in Odisha by Spring Health is a project in Odisha, India, that implements a network of water filter kiosks and a distribution system to supply households with clean water. Using modern solar-powered technology, the kiosks ensure water is safe to drink. Beyond improving health, the project fosters local economic development by engaging community members throughout the water purification and supply process.

GS23392.description: The project is to distribute High efficiency Clean cookstoves(ICS) in Bagmati Zone in Nepal. through the implementation of this project, the Household who use the ICS will significantly reduce the use of firewood for cooking, also reduce the smoke and noxious gas emission as well.

GS23393.description:
The "Avoiding Methane Emissions through Composting at DN Agrar, Romania" project aims to significantly reduce greenhouse gas emissions by implementing controlled aerobic composting of raw dairy manure at two farms located in Alba and Hunedoara counties. Traditionally, manure is managed through open stockpiling or storage in lagoons, practices that lead to uncontrolled anaerobic decomposition and the release of methane (CH₄), a greenhouse gas with a global warming potential significantly higher than CO₂.

By diverting manure from these conventional methods and instead processing it through a structured composting system, the project prevents methane emissions at source. The composting process stabilizes the organic material, producing high-quality compost that can be applied to agricultural land. This not only improves soil health and fertility but also enhances the soil's carbon sequestration capacity, supporting long-term climate resilience in Romanian agriculture.

In summary, the project delivers both immediate climate benefits through methane avoidance and broader environmental co-benefits by promoting sustainable manure management and improving local soil systems.

GS23397.description: This is a Programme of Activities (PoA) called "GS PoA for Sustainable Rice Cultivation Projects in India" in India that will include various Voluntary Project Activities (VPAs) in it. The "GS PoA for Sustainable Rice Cultivation Projects in India" consists of implementation of Alternate and Wetting and Drying (AWD) practice in India. Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) method and aerobic rice cultivation method is a scientifically proven way of managing rice fields for better water management and achieving reduction or avoidance of methane emissions that is caused in traditional submerged rice fields. Therefore, Landmark Agri Exports Pvt. Ltd. (an Indian entity) & WeAct Pty Ltd. (an Australian entity) has taken a voluntary initiative to develop a project in India that is designed specifically for Rice fields to adopt AWD and other adjusted water managements methods, to be implemented across various states of India. Thus, the main objective of the project is to avoid flooded irrigation in rice fields and adopt AWD/other adjusted water management methods for rice cultivation to reduce methane emissions from the rice fields.

GS23398.description:
The proposed project activity is the voluntary action undertaken by Landmark Agri Exports Pvt. Ltd., and WeAct Pty Ltd. The project falls under the Agriculture category introducing improved agricultural practices in rice cultivation.

This project aims to reduce methane (CH4) emissions through improved water management practices involving alternate wetting and drying (AWD) of the paddy lands. AWD is a proven method to reduce CH4 emission by as much as 48% compared to continuously flooded conditions where high rates of CH4 are emitted by the lands due to the anaerobic decomposition of the organic matter . Rice is the most prominent food crop in India. It is the backbone of livelihood for millions of rural households and plays a vital role in the country's food security. India is one of the world's largest producers and exporters of rice and hence plays an important part in the country's economy. The proposed VPA activity is planned to be implemented in the Madhya Pradesh State of India.

This VPA is implemented in Seoni district covering 26,103 ha in 8 tahsils

GS23399.description: The proposed Programme of Activities (PoA) involves the production of biomass briquettes, with the objective of replacing conventional fossil fuels such as coal, furnace oil, and firewood commonly used by industries and institutions for thermal energy applications. The primary goal is to promote the use of clean, renewable, and sustainable biomass energy while reducing reliance on carbon-intensive fuels. Each Voluntary Project Activity (VPA) under this PoA will involve the manufacture of briquettes using agricultural residues and other organic biomass waste, which are typically discarded or left to decompose, resulting in methane emissions and environmental degradation. By converting this waste into high-density fuel briquettes, the PoA addresses key environmental and economic challenges. It contributes to greenhouse gas emission reductions by displacing fossil fuels and preventing methane emissions from un-managed biomass waste. The initiative also supports improved waste management through the productive use of agricultural residues, offers access to cleaner-burning fuels for small and medium-sized industrial units, and generates local employment across the biomass value chain—from raw material collection and processing to transportation and distribution. Additionally,by reducing the use of coal and wood, the PoA helps improve air quality and public health through lower emissions of particulate matter and other harmful pollutants.

GS23400.description: The proposed project involves the production and supply of approximately 10,200 tonnes of biomass briquettes annually, with the objective of replacing conventional fossil fuels such as coal, furnace oil, and firewood that are commonly used by industries and institutions for thermal energy applications. The primary goal is to promote the use of clean, renewable, and sustainable biomass energy while reducing reliance on carbon-intensive fuels. These briquettes are manufactured using agricultural residues and other organic biomass waste, which are typically discarded or left to decompose, resulting in methane emissions and environmental degradation. By converting this waste into high-density fuel briquettes, the project addresses key environmental and economic challenges. The initiative also supports improved waste management through the productive use of agricultural residues, offers access to cleaner-burning fuels for small and medium-sized industrial units, and generates local employment across the biomass value chain—from raw material collection and processing to transportation and distribution. Additionally,by reducing the use of coal and wood, the project helps improve air quality and public health through lower emissions of particulate matter and other harmful pollutants.

GS23401.description:
The PoA aims to reduce methane emissions from irrigated paddy fields by implementing the Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) technique. 
Additionally, AWD offers a variety of socio-economic and environmental advantages. It allows farmers to decrease water consumption while maintaining crop yields, thereby improving water management and enhancing overall water access. Overall, the PoA will contribute to reduced greenhouse gas emissions, promote sustainable farming practices, and support environmental and economic sustainability.

GS23402.description:
The VPA aims to reduce methane emissions from irrigated paddy fields by implementing the Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) technique. Unlike traditional continuous flooding methods, AWD involves intermittent flooding, allowing fields to dry at certain intervals. This approach significantly reduces methane production while also lowering water consumption, making it both environmentally, socially and economically beneficial.
In addition to promoting AWD, the VPA will support participating farmers with a comprehensive package of best practices tailored to optimize rice cultivation in the region.

GS23408.description:
The project includes installation of improved cook stoves and safe drinking water devices in the rural communities of Jumla and Kalikot district of Nepal. 
The Improved Cook Stoves suitable to the cooking patterns and geographical conditions and having greater efficiencies will be chosen for implementation. The use of Improved Cook Stoves significantly reduces fuelwood consumption leading to lower greenhouse gas emissions and improves the indoor air quality.
Additionally, the water filter reduce the risk of waterborne disease by removing harmful bacteria and viruses from drinking water. The water filter removes harmful contaminants from drinking water, balance the pH of  drinking water and ensures safe drinking water.

This project aims to enhance environmental sustainability and improve the health and socio-economic conditions of rural and urban communities in Madagascar. By replacing traditional open-fire cooking methods with improved cookstoves, the project will significantly reduce fuel consumption, thereby decreasing deforestation rates and promoting the sustainable management of natural resources. The project aligns with the Gold Standard's objectives of delivering real, measurable, and long-term emission reductions and promoting sustainable development benefits.

GS23410.description:
BIWACALI stands for Burka Initiative for Water Balancing, Carbon Sequestration and Livelihood Improvement. The Oromo word "Burquaa" means "burbling spring", symbolizing the main objective of this project: ensuring the water security of the West-Ethiopian Upper Dabana - and the East-Ethiopian Hakim Gara watersheds by restoring about 10,000 ha areas degraded area into forest over the next decades. This will be achieved by tree planting and applying the Farmer Managed Natural Regeneration (FMNR) technique, which is designed to significantly improve the income and livelihoods of local farming communities. 

Next to the physical restoration work, major project activities are the formation of cooperatives and unions for forest management and training on FMNR, sustainable farming methods and alternative livelihoods. The newly created cooperatives will be strongly supported by World Vision Ethiopia in the first years of the project. It is envisioned that afterwards, they will take on the main responsibility for managing the forest areas, their products and the monitoring of the project impacts. 

The project is being implemented jointly by the local communities, Heineken Ethiopia, World Vision Ethiopia and FORLIANCE.

GS23411.description: The Programme of Activities (PoA), titled 'Sustainable Rice Production in South East and South Asia', is a multi-country initiative that promotes the adoption of a suite of sustainable agricultural practices. The project's core measure is Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD), a climate-smart irrigation technique aimed at reducing methane emissions and conserving water in rice fields. While initial implementation is focused on rice-growing regions in Indonesia and Vietnam, the project is designed with a long-term vision to scale across other countries in South and Southeast Asia. The primary goal is to generate quantifiable carbon and water benefits, with a broader aim to improve the overall environmental and social sustainability of rice farming by incorporating measures that address soil health, energy efficiency, and pollution control.

GS23412.description: The VPA for Indonesia, a foundational component of the overarching PoA, focuses on promoting sustainable rice production. The project's core activity is the implementation of Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) to reduce methane emissions and conserve water. Serving as the primary pilot for the Rize business model, the VPA leverages a digital platform and on-ground technical support to ensure effective AWD adoption among smallholder farmers. The project aims to improve yields, reduce input costs, and generate a verifiable carbon asset stream that contributes to Indonesia's climate commitments while providing additional income for participating farmers.

GS23413.description: The VPA for Vietnam, a component of the overarching PoA, focuses specifically on promoting sustainable rice production in the country. The project's core activity is the implementation of Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) to reduce methane emissions and conserve water. By providing farmers with training and technical support, the VPA aims to improve yields, reduce input costs, and create a verifiable carbon asset stream that contributes to the country's climate commitments and generates additional income for participating farmers.

GS23414.description: The proposed PoA (Industrial boiler fuel switch- Biomass waste recycling and reuse in East Africa) has been developed by Lean Energy Solutions Limited with the purpose of displacing the use of fossil fuel in manufacturing facilities in East Africa. The project will recycle biomass waste and reuse it in firing biomass boilers, replacing fossil fuel as fuel for thermal energy production. This will displace a proportion of the fossil fuel that the factories currently burn.

GS23415.description: The proposed VPA (Industrial boiler fuel switch in Kenya) has been developed by Lean Energy Solutions Limited with the purpose of displacing the use of fossil fuel in manufacturing facilities in Kenya. The project will recycle biomass waste and reuse it in firing biomass boilers, replacing fossil fuel as fuel for thermal energy production. This will displace a proportion of the fossil fuel that the factories currently burn.

GS23418.description: The project seeks to promote agroforestry in rural areas of India. The project's focus is to improve livelihood of the farmer community by enhancing their social and economic status. The project will not only remove carbon dioxide from the atmosphere but will also help in building climate resilience among the farming community. The agroforestry system will improve soil fertility, reduce erosion, enhance water retention, and increase resilience to climate shocks such as drought and flooding. The project avoids environmental degradation by reducing synthetic fertilizer dependency and preventing land degradation.

GS23420.description:
The Durable Solutions Congo: Clean energy and environmental resilience in the DRC, is a Programme of Activities (PoA) whose purpose is to improve access to efficient cookstoves and safe water supply technologies for low-income households in  rural and peri-urban areas throughout the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). The technologies distributed under this PoA aim to address pressing environmental, health and social challenges in a locally appropriate manner. 
Serving as the starting point, the real-case VPA intends to contribute towards the goals of the PoA by distributing the "Sala Makala Stove," a Top-Lit Up-Draft (TLUD) stove capable of combusting firewood more efficiently than traditional/3-stone biomass cookstoves. Thereby saving approximately 2.04 tCO2e per household per year. The project further aims to improve air quality and subsequently, household health, by reducing exposure to harmful smoke, as well as reducing fuelwood consumption with greater stove efficiency.

GS23421.description:
The purpose of the VPA is to distribute Improved cookstoves in households and communities of Rwanda, Africa. The Improved cookstoves are distributed to households/institutions which were earlier using wood and/or charcoal on rudimentary stoves for cooking/boiling. The project makes the end-users energy efficient and reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions otherwise resulting from the  burning of large amount of non-renewable woody biomass and/or charcoal in baseline scenario. 
The project boundary is the geographical boundary of Rwanda, Africa where the Improved cookstoves are proposed to be distributed.

GS23422.description:
The purpose of the VPA is to distribute Safe water filters in households and communities of Rwanda, Africa. The water filters are distributed to households/institutions which were earlier using wood and/or charcoal on rudimentary stoves for boiling water or were using unsafe water directly without boiling. The project makes the end-users energy efficient and reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions otherwise resulting from the burning of large amount of non-renewable woody biomass and/or charcoal in baseline scenario. 
The project boundary is the geographical boundary of Rwanda, Africa where the safe water filters are proposed to be distributed.

GS23423.description:
The FS BECCS project, proposed under the Gold Standard for Global Goals (GS4GG), reflects FS – Fueling Sustainability's ambition to lead Brazil's energy transition with innovation, technical excellence, and private investment. Founded in 2017, FS is the third-largest ethanol producer in the country, operating modern plants in Mato Grosso.

At its Lucas do Rio Verde facility, FS will capture biogenic CO₂ from corn ethanol fermentation. The stream, with about 98% purity, will be compressed, dehydrated, and injected into deep geological formations of the Parecis Basin for secure, long-term storage. As this CO₂ originates from the atmosphere via photosynthesis, its storage delivers net carbon removals.

Project development followed four phases: Phase 1 (2019–2020) confirmed storage potential through feasibility studies and 2D seismic data. Phase 2 (2020–2022) added a 3D seismic survey and design of capture and compression systems. Phase 3 (2022–2024) drilled a stratigraphic well, collected geological data, and began equipment procurement. Phase 4 (2024–2026), now underway, includes injectivity tests, well conversion, monitoring infrastructure, and capture system construction. Commercial operations are expected in 2025, with carbon injection June 2026.

GS23431.description: The MuLaKiLa project is a long-term (32 years) community-based landscape restoration and climate resilience initiative in Rwanda's western province, spanning Ngororero and Rutsiro districts. As part of the voluntary carbon market, it is projected to sequester 5.4 million tons of CO₂e, with 4.356 million tons of CO₂e accounted for after buffer deduction. The project will restore 21,000 hectares of degraded smallholder land through agroforestry systems, woodlots, and Sustainable Agriculture Land Management (SALM) practices. It will benefit around 160,000 farmers by creating green jobs, improving livelihoods, and addressing climate challenges such as soil erosion, land degradation, and biodiversity loss. Core interventions include planting over 6 million trees, community mobilization, capacity building, and the establishment of innovative nature-based financial mechanisms.

GS23432.description: The project initiative in Timor Leste is designed to enhance socio-economic resilience while reducing local communities' vulnerability to natural disasters. By integrating plantation practices with existing land use practices of the communities, the project aims to restore degraded land, enhance livelihood security through agroforestry, sequester carbon, and strengthen ecosystem-based natural resource management.

GS23433.description: The Future Radici Programme of Activities (PoA) represents a voluntary, long-term climate and biodiversity initiative developed and managed by Leone Alato SpA, the Coordinating and Managing Entity (CME). It has been conceived as an afforestation and reforestation (A/R) programme to address the interlinked crises of climate change, biodiversity degradation, and ecosystem loss. By planting native, long-cycle, non-invasive trees within the Leone Alato perimeter (Italy end Romania), the overarching aim is to contribute substantively to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), with a principal focus on SDG 13 (Climate Action) through the biological removal and long-term storage of atmospheric carbon dioxide via A/R practices. In doing so, the PoA also contributes to SDG 15 (Life on Land) through the restoration of degraded ecosystems and the strengthening of biodiversity, as well as to SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production) by reducing synthetic fertilizers and pesticides, and SDG 5 (Gender Equality) by generating inclusive and equitable socioeconomic opportunities within local communities.

GS23434.description: "SCIF Schools Drinking Water Project" aims to provide safe drinking water to schools and communities in Rwanda. The project consists of the installation of rainwater harvesting tanks and fitting of water filtration systems. By installing tanks with filtration systems school children, staff and their families will be able to access clean drinking water. This reduces the need for the school and households to boil water as a means of purification or consume unsafe water which is the scenario prior to implementation of the project activity. The project will be small scale, and the emission reductions achieved due to avoidance of fuel used for boiling water will be certified by the Gold Standard.

GS23435.description:
The Real Case VPA Future Radici, Lanuvio represents a pivotal and strategic initiative within the broader framework of the Programme of Activities (PoA) Future Radici. Located in the municipality of Lanuvio (Rome), the project spans a total area of 403.9 hectares across three agricultural estates: Solonio, Presciano, and Campoleone. These lands are owned by Leone Alato SpA. The project envisions the planting of approximately 422,000 trees, with the goal of transforming these agricultural lands into thriving, biodiverse forest ecosystems.
The primary objective of the Real Case of Lanuvio is to establish native and ecologically rich forest environments through a combination of afforestation and agroforestry practices. These practices are carefully tailored to the pedoclimatic and ecological characteristics of each site, ensuring that the interventions enhance biodiversity, support complex habitats, and maximize long-term carbon sequestration. The forest models adopted in this project are non-extractive, the harvesting of timber or biomass is explicitly excluded. This commitment extends for a minimum duration of 60 years.
To quantify the carbon absorption, the project will rely on methodologies recommended by the IPCC (Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change). These methods will be calibrated using national and regional data. The goal is to produce credits that are measurable, verifiable, and directly linked to positive outcomes in both biodiversity and social impact.

GS23436.description: The PoA promotes the use of Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) technology, which delivers both environmental and socio-economic benefits across different districts of Bangladesh. Overall, AWD supports more efficient water management, lower greenhouse gas emissions, encourage sustainable agricultural practices, and contribute to long-term environmental and economic resilience.

GS23439.description: The VPA on sustainable rice cultivation using Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) technology is implemented in Thakurgaon district of Bangladesh. GS23440.description: The VPA aims to reduce methane emissions from rice cultivation through the implementation of the Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) technique. GS23441.description: The sustainable rice cultivation VPA utilizing Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) technology has been initiated in Gazipur district, Bangladesh. GS23447.description:
This project introduces Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) as a climate-smart water management practice in rice farming in Dong Thap Province, a major rice-producing area of the Mekong Delta. The project aims to reduce methane emissions from rice cultivation, save irrigation water, and support sustainable rice production. It is being implemented by Rikolto in Vietnam acting on behalf of Livelihoods Carbon Fund (LCF3).
The core technical intervention of the project is the application of AWD, a water-saving irrigation technique that reduces methane emissions in rice cultivation. Instead of keeping rice paddies continuously flooded, AWD involves allowing the field to dry intermittently, typically until the water level drops 15 cm below the soil surface, at which point irrigation is resumed with a shallow flood of 2–5 cm. This practice reduces the anaerobic conditions in the soil that are responsible for methane generation, without negatively affecting rice yields. 
To support this method, the project installs PVC monitoring tubes (commonly known as pani-pipes) in farmers' fields. These tools allow farmers to visually monitor the water level in the soil and make informed irrigation decisions, making AWD both accessible and easy to implement.
In addition to water management, the project promotes improved straw and fertilizer practices. Rather than incorporating straw into the soil, which significantly contributes to methane emissions, farmers are encouraged to remove, compost, or repurpose straw for other uses such as mushroom cultivation. Fertilizer use is also optimized to improve nitrogen efficiency and reduce emissions of nitrous oxide (N₂O), another potent greenhouse gas.

GS23448.description: SCIF has initiated the GS 12087 PoA "SCIF for Sustainable Living and Public Health Programme" that aims to implement interventions providing safe drinking water to communities in Uganda. The second activity of the PoA "GS12087 GS12088 RVPA-1 Uganda Safe Drinking Water Project, Phase 2" aims provide safe drinking water to rural communities in the districts of Lyantonde, Kalungu and Kabarole. The project consists of the repair of damaged and defunct deep boreholes progressively.

GS23449.description: The PoA aims at implementing sustainable agroforestry practices in agricultural and non-agricultural land in various regions of Tanzania. By integrating plantation practices with existing land use practices of the communities, this strategic initiative will contribute significantly towards carbon sequestration while also delivering additional environmental benefits such as improved soil health, enhanced biodiversity, and increased local employment opportunities.

GS23450.description: The VPA aims at implementing sustainable agroforestry practices in agricultural and non-agricultural land across Tanzania. GS23452.description: Serving as the starting point, the real-case VPA (GS23420) intends to contribute towards the goals of the PoA by distributing the "Sala Makala Stove," a Top-Lit Up-Draft (TLUD) stove capable of combusting firewood more efficiently than traditional/3-stone biomass cookstoves across the Kasai, Kasai Central, and Kasai Oriental provinces. The project further aims to improve air quality and subsequently, household health, by reducing exposure to harmful smoke, as well as reducing fuelwood consumption with greater stove efficiency.

GS23453.description: The primary objective of the Community Initiated Regeneration for Carbon & Livelihoods Enhancement (CIRCLE) project is carbon sequestration and livelihood enhancement through the restoration of degraded lands in Luapula province of Zambia. The project is expected to contribute to climate change mitigation and adaptation through the emission reductions and introduction of alternative livelihood skills across the project area respectively. The alternative livelihood activities are aimed at enhancing income generation among households and thereby reducing their propensity to engage in destructive activities such as charcoal production and conventional agriculture.

GS23454.description: The Khonobod 1-2 Utility-Scale Solar Photovoltaic (PV) Project is a large-scale renewable energy initiative designed to support Uzbekistan's transition toward clean energy and contribute to the global effort to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. The purpose of the project is to generate electricity by using clean solar power resources to meet the national electricity demand. The project will contribute to the reduction of GHG emission by displacing part with fossil fuel fired power plants of the generated electricity by the Grid. The expected annual GHG emission reductions over the first crediting period are 554,070 tCO2e/yr, which will contribute to the alleviation of climate change effects. The Khonobod 1-2 Solar PV Project will contribute to the achievement of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy), SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth) and SDG 13 (Climate Action).

GS23460.description:
The bundled project implemented by AES comprises two renewable power plants: Cristales, which generates electricity exclusively from solar energy, and Pampas, which utilizes both wind and solar resources. Both projects will be located in northern Chile, specifically in the Antofagasta Region, within the Atacama Desert.
The project activities include the construction and operation of the generation plants, each equipped with Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS). The installed capacities for Pampas are 120 MW for wind, 230 MW for PV, and 340 MW for BESS, while for Cristales (previously referred to as Andes III) they are 287 MW for PV and 340 MW for BESS.

GS23462.description:
This Gold Standard Large-Scale (Individual) Project Activity is a voluntary initiative developed by Clean Cooking Technologies S.R.L. (CCT) as the Project Developer. The project will be supported by multiple investors and funding partners. The Host Country for this project is the United Republic of Tanzania, where the activity will be implemented across the country.

The project aims to distribute high-quality induction stoves and electric pressure cookers (collectively referred to as electric cookstoves) to households and communities in Tanzania. Implementation will be led by CCT Tanzania, in collaboration with local organizations. The project will initially be rolled out in Dar es Salaam and subsequently expanded to other regions across Tanzania based on demand.

In Tanzania, a large proportion of households continue to rely on inefficient traditional cooking methods—such as three-stone fires and traditional charcoal stoves—that consume significant amounts of biomass and contribute to deforestation and indoor air pollution. By introducing modern, energy-efficient electric cooking technologies, the project seeks to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, improve indoor air quality, and enhance the overall quality of life for participating households.

The project will be implemented in both rural and urban areas where households have access to electricity.  The project will have a total crediting period of 15 years, comprising an initial 5-year period with two renewals of 5 years each.                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     100 of % distributed induction stoves in the project will be equipped with IoT devices to enable continuous monitoring of energy consumption for cooking and water heating in the households. The project will apply the Gold Standard-approved methodology, "Methodology for Metered & Measured Energy Cooking Devices" (Version 1.2), recognized as the most robust and conservative emission reduction calculation approach for cookstove carbon projects. This methodology is also endorsed by the ICVCM under its Core Carbon Principles (CCP), ensuring transparency and integrity in carbon credit issuance from cookstove projects.

By combining energy-efficient modern elelctric cookstove technology with real-time usage monitoring using the latest IoT device and a rigorous Gold Standard Metered Methodology, and further fNRB value derived from MoFUSS for Tanzania, the project will generate high-quality, high-integrity carbon credits while avoiding any risk of overestimation. The project is also one of the approved project by Sylvera.  

Beyond emissions reduction, the project is designed to deliver substantial co-benefits aligned with many UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), including:
- SDG 1: No Poverty
- SDG 3: Good Health and Well-being
- SDG 4: Quality Education
- SDG 5: Gender Equality
- SDG 7: Affordable and Clean Energy
- SDG 8: Decent Work and Economic Growth
- SDG 12: Responsible Consumption and Production
- SDG 13: Climate Action
- SDG 15: Life on Land
These co-benefits will be formally certified under the Gold Standard framework, reinforcing the project's holistic impact on climate and community resilience.

GS23464.description: Sistema.bio is a social enterprise that provides access to innovative biodigester technology, training and financing to address the challenges of poverty, food security, and climate change. Sistema.bio manufactures and distributes high-quality, affordable biodigesters that enable farmers around the world to convert waste into energy and fertilizer, and works with farmers to ensure they become more sustainable, independent, and productive while mitigating the carbon emissions generated by agricultural activities. This project will provide a wide range of social, economic and environmental benefits for families and communities in India through the installation of biodigesters. The project includes various sizes of biodigesters to adjust to the different types of farmers. The project will focus on smallholder dairy farmers in the country, especially subsistence farmers who typically use woodfuel or LPG for their energy needs both in the household and productive uses in the farm, and who currently do not manage the manure generated by their animals and have either solid or liquid storage practices for this.

GS23468.description: The purpose of the Programme of Activity (PoA) is to provide safe drinking water to households in rural communities. This initiative intends to diminish the reliance on non-renewable biomass for water purification, which would otherwise be necessary in the absence of this project. The project aims to achieve this by deploying automated chlorination units, UV disinfection, and utilizing advanced IoT and AI-ML driven cloud technology for real-time water quality monitoring. The geographical boundary and target are households in rural communities with overhead tank reservoirs that have no definitive chlorination or post UV disinfections. This project will provide online access via App to local inhabitants to monitor their water quality online, on their smart phones, and the distributed water will be free of charge to community. The project is anticipated to yield significant impacts in health, social, environmental, and economic spheres for thousands of individuals in the project area. Furthermore, this project is aligned with various UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) to create a comprehensive positive impact.

The Program of Activities, "Cova Safe Water Program in Central America" will provide safe water to rural communities in Central America with the first carbon project beginning in Honduras.  Cova installs zero-emission water treatment technologies (in-line chlorination) to existing water supply systems.  The resulting safe water replaces the need to burn non-renewable biomass in water boiling for purification of the water.  
This avoidance of fuel combustion reduces Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions and contributes to climate change goals.

GS23472.description: Under this project activity, VISION GREENEN Tech Pvt Ltd is developing an improved cookstoves program "Sustainable Cooking Solutions for Rural Communities: Madhya Pradesh Initiative" and aims to distribute improved cookstoves (ICS) to rural households in the Dhar and Khargone districts of Madhya Pradesh.  The target beneficiaries of the program will be low-income & firewood-using households residing in villages of Dhar and Khargone districts of Madhya Pradesh. The Project intends to reach households that are currently using inefficient traditional cookstoves for cooking their meals. Households will be provided with improved cookstoves. ICS improves the combustion efficiency and thermal transfer to the cooking pot compared with a traditional stove, thereby reducing fuel usage. As a result, this project will contribute to SDGs including  SDG 3 (Good Health and Well Being), SDG 4 (Quality Education), SDG 5 (Gender Equality), SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean energy), SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), SDG 13 (Climate Action) and SDG 15 (Life on Land), in both quantitative and qualitative ways.

GS23475.description:
Carbon Neutral Energy Systems Limited (C-NES) has developed the "Ecofoyer Guinée -  Programme for the Dissemination of Improved and Advanced Cookstoves in Guinea" as a registered Gold Standard Programme of Activities (PoA). The PoA reduces greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and improves household well-being by displacing the use of traditional, inefficient biomass cookstoves with modern, energy-efficient and cleaner alternatives.

The PoA responds to Guinea's NDCs and its significant dependence on traditional cooking practices, which has resulted in widespread deforestation, indoor air pollution, and associated health burdens—especially among women and children. Through the introduction of improved cookstoves (ICS), advanced cookstoves (ACS), and local manufacturing of renewable fuels (biomass pellets) the Ecofoyer Guinée PoA contributes to sustainable energy access, climate mitigation, and social development across urban, peri-urban and rural areas.

Under this country-wide PoA, the initial rollout includes the prefectures of Conakry, N'Zérékoré, Forécariah, and Beyla. The PoA involves the dissemination, monitoring, and maintenance of ICS and ACS technologies that meet defined efficiency and emission performance standards.

GS23476.description:
Carbon Neutral Energy Systems Limited (C-NES) has developed the Ecofoyer Guinée – Programme for the Dissemination of Improved and Advanced Cookstoves in Guinea as a Gold Standard Programme of Activities (PoA). The PoA reduces greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and improve household well-being by displacing traditional, inefficient biomass cookstoves with modern, energy-efficient, and cleaner alternatives.

Through the dissemination of Improved Cookstoves (ICS), Advanced Cookstoves (ACS), and the local production of renewable biomass fuels (pellets), the Ecofoyer Guinée PoA contributes to sustainable energy access, climate change mitigation, and socio-economic development across urban, peri-urban, and rural areas of Guinea.

VPA 01, implemented under this PoA, covers the prefectures of Conakry, N'Zérékoré, Forécariah, and Beyla. The activity involves the dissemination, monitoring, and maintenance of ICS and ACS technologies, as well as the introduction of locally manufactured biomass pellets as a renewable fuel alternative. Implementation will be carried out through partnerships with Local Implementation Partners (LIPs) responsible for distribution, user training, awareness campaigns, and after-sales support.

This first VPA serves as the real-case example for the PoA, demonstrating the operational model, monitoring framework, and sustainable development co-benefits expected from future VPAs to be included under the Ecofoyer Guinée Programme.

GS23478.description:
The Electric Cooking Program in Bangladesh by ATEC aims to replace highly polluting non-renewable and fossil cooking fuels with clean, efficient electric cooking solutions. The project will distribute and install ATEC's patented eCook—an electric cookstove equipped with GSM connectivity that enables 100% digital MRV through ATEC's dashboard. The primary beneficiaries are households that currently cook with biomass but are already connected to the national grid.

By transitioning to efficient electric cooking, the project will offer households an affordable, convenient, and safe cooking alternative while contributing to SDGs 1, 3, 5, 7, 8, and 13.

Project Description:
Distribution and installation of eCook units with GSM and 100% dMRV capabilities.
ATEC will lead project development and implementation and local implementation partners will support VPA management in Bangladesh.
The project is voluntary and will apply the Methodology for Metered & Measured Energy Cooking Devices v1.2 for calculating emission reductions.

The project will replace unsustainable biomass-based cooking—often practiced on inefficient three-stone fires and traditional stoves—with efficient electric cookstoves, thereby reducing GHG emissions and negative environmental and health impacts.

GS23487.description:
The goal of the "Community Program for the Preservation and Restoration of Mangroves" is to implement projects for the restoration of degraded mangrove and coastal/freshwater wetlands ecosystems. The aim is to recover ecological functionality by re-establishing hydrological connectivity, improving biodiversity, and removing atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO₂) through natural carbon sequestration processes.
VPAs included under the PoA will be selected where degradation is demonstrated and restoration is technically feasible, prioritizing actions such as hydrological reconnection, assisted natural regeneration, and targeted enrichment planting with native species, together with the maintenance and monitoring required for durable outcomes. The aim is to restore ecological processes (water exchange, sediment dynamics, recruitment), enhance biodiversity, and remove CO₂ through conservative, verified sequestration in line with Gold Standard requirements.
