GS23556.description:
The main objectives of this project are to provide water treatment to schools in Rwanda to address microbiological contamination, and avoid CO2e emissions associated with water treatment.
This project will address critical access to safe water, whilst contributing to pollution reduction through the benefits of carbon financing. The water purification systems will reduce both the use of and demand for firewood and other fuels used to boil drinking water, leading to the reduction of carbon dioxide emissions. The project activities managed by Virridy will distribute, install, and service low GHG emitting water purification systems at point-of-use (POU) to provide safe drinking water (SDW) for institutional application at schools. The project technology will be installed at the POU within facilities of the schools (mostly, primary and secondary schools, other educational institutions can be included).

GS23557.description: The voluntary project activity (VPA) is a voluntary initiative by Unlocking Communities (UC) to distribute improved charcoal stoves in Haiti. The target beneficiaries under the project will be the households which were earlier dependent on charcoal based traditional stoves for cooking. Unlocking Communities is a locally run organization working in northern and central Haiti. Distribution of improved cookstove which is a clean energy product as compared to the baseline, will reduce the GHG emissions.  The use of improved cookstove will offer several environmental and health benefits such as reduction in the levels of indoor air pollution (IAP), women drudgery, deforestation etc. thereby having a positive impact on the health of the community.

GS23559.description:
The IRIBA Water Access Program in Rwanda (IWAP Rwanda) is a transformative climate and health initiative bringing clean, carbon-free drinking water to underserved schools and communities across Rwanda.
Implemented by IRIBA Water Group, the program will install 2,500 smart water ATMs providing safe, affordable drinking water to over 1 million people who need it most. These innovative water points eliminate the need to boil water with firewood or charcoal, directly reducing greenhouse gas emissions while preventing deforestation and improving public health.

GS23560.description:
The Kuphatana project aims to reforest 1,000 hectares of highly degraded land in the Administrative Post of Murraça, Mozambique, to restore the local ecosystem and support the socio-economic development of nearby communities. The project adopts a participatory approach, integrating environmental restoration with diversified livelihood activities such as beekeeping and dried mango production to ensure long-term sustainability and community engagement.
Climate change mitigation/adaptation contributions
Carbon Sequestration: The project establishes a forest that serves as a carbon sink, sequestering an annual average of 8,925 tCO2e. Over the 40-year crediting period, the total estimated net benefit is 351,044.5 tCO2e.
Biodiversity Enhancement: By planting a mix of native species (Vachellia xanthophloea and Khaya anthotheca) alongside non-invasive Eucalyptus urophylla, the project restores habitats for local flora and fauna
Climate Adaptation through Livelihoods - Beekeeping: The project engages 15 families per year from adjacent villages, providing them with beehives and training. This creates a direct economic incentive for the community to protect the forest from threats such as uncontrolled fires or illegal deforestation, as the bee colonies rely on the trees for nectar.
Climate Adaptation through Livelihoods - Sustainable Value Chains: Establishing a local value chain for dried mangoes offers diversified, climate-resilient financial growth for local families.

GS23562.description:
The project aims to support the energy transition and reduce charcoal consumption and related greenhouse gas emissions through the distribution of improved charcoal cookstoves and pellet gasifier cookstoves within local communities. By promoting the adoption of cleaner and more efficient cooking technologies, the project contributes to lowering fuel demand, improving energy efficiency, and reducing environmental and climate impacts associated with traditional cooking practices.



In parallel, the project places strong emphasis on community empowerment by creating local employment opportunities, delivering technical and operational training, and investing in essential community infrastructure such as water towers and greenhouses. These activities are designed to strengthen local capacities, improve access to resources, and foster sustainable socio-economic development in the countries where the project is implemented.



The project contributes to the achievement of the following Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs): SDG 1 (No Poverty), SDG 2 (Zero Hunger) SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-Being), SDG 4 (Quality Education), SDG 5 (Gender Equality), SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation), SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy), SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), SDG 13 (Climate Action), and SDG 15 (Life on Land).

GS23567.description: The Gold Standard "Nestlé & FNC Tree Planting Colombia" is a joint strategy between Nestlé and the National Federation of Coffee Growers of Colombia (FNC). It is implemented through the planting of trees on coffee farms that are part of Nestlé's value chain and on neighboring farms located within the coffee-growing ecosystem. The project emerged as a mitigation and adaptation measure to prepare crops for the impacts of climate variability, contribute to the conservation of water and soils, enhance biodiversity, and serve as a nature-based solution for the removal of CO₂ from the atmosphere.

GS23572.description:
This VPA aims to support the energy transition and reduce charcoal consumption and related greenhouse gas emissions through the distribution of improved charcoal cookstoves and pellet gasifier cookstoves, applying a fuel-switch approach. By promoting the adoption of cleaner and more efficient cooking solutions, the VPA contributes to reducing reliance on traditional charcoal and lowering associated environmental and climate impacts.



The VPA will be implemented in Zambia, with a particular focus on the Copperbelt region, targeting urban and peri-urban areas. The activities are designed to generate positive impacts within local communities, with specific attention to supporting women's empowerment through improved access to clean cooking technologies, reduced time spent on fuel collection, and enhanced livelihood opportunities.

In addition, the VPA includes the construction of water towers to ensure reliable access to safe drinking water, along with continuous capacity-building activities aimed at strengthening local skills, knowledge, and long-term socio-economic resilience.

GS23573.description: The voluntary project activity (VPA) is a voluntary initiative by Unlocking Communities (UC) to distribute institution water filters in Haiti. The target beneficiaries under the project will be the institutions like schools which were earlier dependent on boiling using non-renewable biomass for safe drinking water. Unlocking Communities is a locally run organization working in northern and central Haiti. Distribution of institutional water filters which is a clean energy product as compared to the baseline, will reduce the GHG emissions by eliminating the need for water treatment through boiling.  The use of water filters will offer several environmental and health benefits such as reduction in the levels of indoor air pollution (IAP), reduction in water borne diseases, deforestation etc. thereby having a positive impact on the health of the community.

GS23574.description: The voluntary project activity (VPA) is a voluntary initiative by Unlocking Communities (UC) to distribute household water filters in Haiti. The target beneficiaries under the project will be the households which were earlier dependent on boiling using non-renewable biomass for safe drinking water. Unlocking Communities is a locally run organization working in northern and central Haiti. Distribution of household water filters which is a clean energy product as compared to the baseline, will reduce the GHG emissions by eliminating the need for water treatment through boiling.  The use of water filters will offer several environmental and health benefits such as reduction in the levels of indoor air pollution (IAP), reduction in water borne diseases, deforestation etc. thereby having a positive impact on the health of the community.

GS23582.description: The proposed GS project activity "CGR Guatapara Landfill Project" promotes destruction and utilization of landfill gas (LFG) (rich in methane) generated at the CGR Guatapará landfill, located in the municipality of Guatapará in São Paulo State (South-eastern region of Brazil). LFG destruction and utilization occurs through its collection and destruction in high temperature enclosed flare(s) and its utilization as gaseous fuel for electricity generation (in engine-generator sets installed at the CGR Guatapará landfill as part of the project activity) respectively. Thus, besides methane destruction, the project activity also promotes generation of electricity by using renewable energy source.

GS23590.description: The project activity titled "Proactiva CGA Iperó Landfill Gas to Energy Project" encompasses the promotion of destruction and utilization landfill gas (LFG) (rich in methane) at the CGA Iperó landfill site. LFG destruction occurs in a high temperature enclosed flare and through its utilization as gaseous fuel for electricity generation (in engine-generator sets). Thus, besides methane destruction, the project activity also promotes generation of electricity by using renewable energy sources (with a total nameplate capacity of about 8.5 MW). The CGA Iperó landfill is located located in the border of Sorocaba and Iperó's municipalities, in São Paulo State, Southeastern Region of Brazil.

GS23591.description: This VPA deploys efficient improved cookstoves (ICS), reducing woody biomass consumption for Urban and peri-urban households in the Republic of Zambia. The scenario existing prior to the implementation of the project is the use of very inefficient traditional cookstoves or 3- stone fires, consuming a lot of non-renewable charcoal and firewood. The high biomass consumption has negative impacts on the environment leading to deforestation and land degradation, Greenhouse Gas Emissions (GHG) emissions, loss of soil fertility and soils' reduced ability of water retention. Further, indoor air pollution through health-damaging pollutants while combusting firewood and charcoal result in diseases like e.g. pneumonia, stroke, ischemic heart diseases, chronic obstructive pulmonary diseases and lung cancer.

GS23593.description: The Büyükkışla WPP Project with BESS is designed by Entek Elektrik Üretim A.Ş. as a strategic intervention to increase Türkiye's renewable energy capacity while addressing the inherent stability challenges of wind power. The primary objective is to generate 350,049,600 kWh of clean electricity annually, thereby significantly reducing the carbon intensity of the national grid. By displacing fossil fuel-based generation, the project plays a vital role in climate change mitigation, helping to lower greenhouse gas emissions and preserving finite natural resources such as coal and natural gas. Beyond mere power generation, the integration of advanced storage technology ensures that this renewable energy is utilized efficiently, contributing to the broader goal of a low-carbon and energy-independent economy.

GS23596.description: The programme of activities (PoA) is a voluntary initiative of Westwind Energy Sarl to distribute improved cookstoves (ICS) to households and institutions across rural and urban areas of Senegal. The target beneficiaries of the clean cooking initiative under the programme will be those households that were earlier dependent on traditional stoves or three stone fire stoves for preparing their meals. Westwind will ensure that an improved cooking technology distributed under the programme is accessible to all the end users covered under this PoA. The improved cookstoves will offer several environmental benefits such as reduction in the levels of indoor air pollution (IAP) thereby having a positive impact on the health of the community.

GS23597.description: The project will distribute improved wood stoves to the households in rural areas of Senegal which were earlier dependent on conventional stoves for cooking. The project will make the end-users energy efficient that will reduce greenhouse gas emissions otherwise resulting from the burning of non-renewable biomass for preparing meals. Westwind will ensure that an improved cooking technology distributed under the programme is accessible to all the end users covered under this PoA. The improved cookstoves will offer several environmental benefits such as reduction in the levels of indoor air pollution (IAP) thereby having a positive impact on the health of the community.

GS23598.description: The project will distribute improved charcoal stoves to the households in urban areas of Senegal which were earlier dependent on conventional stoves for cooking. The project will make the end-users energy efficient that will reduce greenhouse gas emissions otherwise resulting from the burning of non-renewable biomass for preparing meals. Westwind will ensure that an improved cooking technology distributed under the programme is accessible to all the end users covered under this PoA. The improved cookstoves will offer several environmental benefits such as reduction in the levels of indoor air pollution (IAP) thereby having a positive impact on the health of the community.

GS23612.description:
The Program Development Objective is to (i) reduce carbon emission and cost of operation for Thailand, (ii) improve air quality, and (iii) tap into the potential of the carbon market to offset the cost of investments with short-term and no regret interventions that are proposed to be implemented in the coming years to enable immediate actions of stakeholders to move towards a green and climate-resilient future. The program aims to support Thailand to reduce carbon emissions and move towards a green and climate resilient future through the following interventions:
•	Increasing renewable energy (RE) generation capacity for captive consumption
•	Improving energy efficiency (EE) in buildings
•	Upgrading to LED streetlights 
•	Transition to electric vehicles

GS23613.description:
The proposed VPA aims to increase renewable energy generation capacity via solar photovoltaic (PV) installation in public and private buildings. Thailand has immense potential for solar-based projects. While large-scale solar farms require large land-use, rooftop solar can utilize the space on the rooftops of buildings or in and around as captive ground-mounted solar installations within the premises of the buildings in cities. Thus, installing solar for buildings is a practical measure to reduce emissions and energy demand for cities.
The VPA entails the installation of rooftop and ground-mounted solar PV systems for captive (self-consumption) use in Thailand. The VPA will generate approximately 20,126 MWh annually and achieve 8,030 tCO2 in annual emission reductions.

GS23620.description:
KPC intends to develop a bamboo plantation designed to address socio-economic and environmental challenges in the Philippines.  Bamboo is known for its high carbon sequestration capabilities.  One of our goals is to contribute to greenhouse gas (GHG) removals thereby generating high integrity carbon credits representing verified greenhouse gas removals over the crediting period and also providing jobs and economic returns to the IP communities.

The geographic region of the project is in Cotabato province in the Philippines within the two Municipalities of President Roxas and Arakan. The project will be implemented on IPs' ancestral lands within the defined project boundary.

The project will provide a sustainable and steady source of livelihood for IP communities that will help address rural poverty and will provide the new generation of IP's better opportunities in life. It will foster rural development, strengthen food security, and promote social stability through sustainable employment generation. It will also foster collaboration between the private and public sectors to further develop the Philippine bamboo industry.

GS23626.description: The Granadillos Wind Park project consists of the development of a 50 MW wind power facility located in Villa Vázquez, Montecristi province, aimed at supplying renewable electricity to the national grid. The project is expected to generate approximately 153 GWh annually using wind turbines. It will contribute to climate change mitigation (SDG 13) and support access to affordable and clean energy (SDG 7). Additionally, it will promote economic growth and job creation (SDG 8), generating up to 350 jobs during construction and around 15 permanent positions during operation and maintenance.

GS23627.description: The Matafongo Solar Park project consists of the development of a 50 MWac photovoltaic facility located in Sabana Buey village, Peravia province, aimed at supplying renewable electricity to the national grid (SENI). The project is expected to generate approximately 118 GWh annually and reduce around 80,000 tCO₂e per year. It will contribute to climate change mitigation (SDG 13) and support access to affordable and clean energy (SDG 7). Additionally, it will promote economic growth and job creation (SDG 8), generating up to 350 jobs during construction and around 15 permanent positions during operation and maintenance.

GS23629.description: The primary objective of this project is to rehabilitate broken and non-functional boreholes to provide clean and safe drinking water to local communities in Malawi. This initiative addresses the need for alternative water purification methods, reducing the reliance on boiling water for drinking purposes and thereby improving the living conditions of the population. The project alleviates the burden on rural women and children, who often bear the responsibility of collecting water and firewood by ensuring access to clean drinking water within 1 kilometre of households. Consequently, this project reduces carbon dioxide emissions associated with the combustion process traditionally used for water purification. In addition to its environmental impact, the project significantly enhances the quality of life, health, and socio-economic status of beneficiaries in the water-stressed regions of Malawi. It includes hygiene awareness campaigns to improve sanitation among local inhabitants. Furthermore, it creates employment opportunities for young people through installing and maintaining rehabilitated boreholes.

GS23645.description:
The EOS Climate – High-Integrity Climate & Social Impact Programme is a Programme of Activities (PoA) developed under the Gold Standard for the Global Goals (GS4GG) framework, aligned with the Paris Agreement. The Programme is coordinated and managed by EOS Climate as the Coordinating and Managing Entity (CME).
The Programme addresses greenhouse gas emissions associated with the use of non-renewable biomass fuels for boiling and sterilizing water in rural and peri-urban communities across Malawi. In the baseline scenario, households rely on unsafe water sources and boil water using firewood or charcoal, resulting in adverse health impacts, time burdens on women and children, local deforestation, and significant GHG emissions.
The Programme enables access to safe, reliable, and continuous drinking water through the installation of solar-powered artesian borehole systems with communal tap stands. All project activities operate with zero direct GHG emissions, eliminating the need for biomass combustion at the point of water use.
The geographical boundary is national in scope, covering eligible rural and peri-urban areas across Malawi. Individual Voluntary Project Activities (VPAs) are developed and included under the PoA framework over time, in accordance with Gold Standard requirements.

GS23647.description: The Wells of Life – Sustainable Safe Water for Malawi is a voluntary carbon mitigation Programme of Activities (PoA) registered under the Gold Standard for the Global Goals (GS4GG), coordinated and managed by EOS Climate and Energy Ltd as the Coordinating and Managing Entity (CME). The Programme is designed to improve continuous access to safe and reliable drinking water in underserved communities in Malawi, while reducing greenhouse gas emissions associated with the boiling of drinking water using non-renewable biomass fuels. VPA-1, the first real case Voluntary Project Activity under the PoA, covers 19 solar-powered groundwater well systems implemented across the Southern Region of Malawi, spanning the districts of Machinga, Zomba, Mulanje, Thyolo, and Blantyre. The Programme applies the Safe Drinking Water Supply (SDWS v2.0) methodology and contributes to SDG 3, 5, 6, 7, 13, and 15. No financial burden is placed on end-users; access to safe drinking water is provided free of charge to beneficiary communities.

GS23659.description:
The PoA "Water for People – Clean Water Access Programme in Africa" targets peri-urban and rural communities and institutions in Rwanda, Malawi, and Uganda, where many still rely on unsafe water sources and purify their water by boiling it over wood-fueled stoves. Across these three countries, existing water infrastructure is often inadequate or in disrepair due to limited maintenance capacity and insufficient water treatment.

Under this PoA, Water For People, in collaboration with government authorities and community WASH committees, will install, rehabilitate, and maintain thousands of water points in each country to deliver reliable, safe water to communities and institutions. By providing safe drinking water without the need for fuel, the programme directly reduces greenhouse gas emissions while improving health and livelihoods.

GS23660.description:
The Madzi Clean Water Project targets peri-urban and rural communities in Malawi, where many households and institutions still rely on collecting unsafe water and purifying it by boiling over wood-fueled stoves. This practice generates greenhouse gas emissions and exposes families to harmful indoor air pollution. Providing safe drinking water without the need for fuel will directly reduce emissions while improving health and livelihoods across participating communities.

Many existing water sources in Malawi are either inadequate or in disrepair due to limited maintenance capacity and insufficient water treatment. Under this Voluntary Programme of Activity, Water For People, in collaboration with local government authorities and water committees, will install, rehabilitate, and maintain water points to deliver reliable, safe water to communities.

GS23661.description:
The Ubuzima Clean Water Project targets peri-urban and rural communities in Rwanda, where many households and institutions still rely on collecting unsafe water and purifying it by boiling over wood-fueled stoves. This practice generates greenhouse gas emissions and exposes families to harmful indoor air pollution. Providing safe drinking water without the need for fuel will directly reduce emissions while improving health and livelihoods across participating communities.

Many existing water sources in Rwanda are either inadequate or in disrepair due to limited maintenance capacity and insufficient water treatment. Under this Voluntary Programme of Activity, Water For People, in collaboration with government authorities and local operators, will install, rehabilitate, and maintain water points to deliver reliable, safe water to communities.

GS23676.description: The Belize Coastal Sargassum Resilience and Circularity Project aims to intercept and process sargassum biomass and eligible biodegradable organic matter to avoid methane emissions from uncontrolled decomposition and landfill disposal. The project combines controlled aerobic treatment, decentralized organic waste processing, and circular resource recovery to transform intercepted biomass into beneficial products, including biochar-enriched compost for local use. Implemented initially in Caye Caulker, Belize, in collaboration with local stakeholders, the project is designed to strengthen coastal resilience, support sustainable land management, reduce environmental impacts associated with sargassum accumulation, and contribute to measurable climate mitigation outcomes under Gold Standard methodologies.

ISOprj_1H502CZZH1S0VMYW.methodology: Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement from Coastal Outfalls
ISOprj_1H502CZZH1S0VMYW.description: Planetary removes carbon by adding finely ground alkaline feedstock to industrial outfalls that discharge into the ocean. This reduces ocean acidity and allows the ocean to naturally absorb more CO₂ from the atmosphere through air-sea gas exchange.

ISOprj_1HCHT9G2H1S05MYP.description: Deep Sky Alpha is a testing facility that evaluates the energy consumption, operability, and reliability of various direct air capture technologies under real-world conditions. The project encompasses the capture, liquefaction, transport, and sequestration of CO₂. CO₂ captured at Alpha is transported by road and sequestered off-site.

ISOprj_1HHYZFVGW1S044ZY.description: Vaulted is a BiCRS solution, taking end-of-life organic waste that otherwise would have decomposed, and geologically sequestering the waste for storage. Vaulted secures a range of end-of-life organic wastes (including biosolids, livestock and agricultural waste, paper sludge, and others) through sustainable sourcing practices, and deploys slurry injection technology to geologically sequester these wastes for the purpose of permanent carbon removal.

ISOprj_1HZSSWBQM1S08H83.description: Charm Industrial converts biomass residues (for example, corn stover, forestry residues) into bio-oil by heating the biomass quickly to very high temperatures. Charm uses woody or cellulosic residues in their pyrolysis and ensures that any emissions associated with growth or harvesting of this biomass are accounted for. This means waste biomass that would have otherwise decomposed is a preferred feedstock. The resulting bio-oil is low in energy content, but high in carbon content, and can be injected underground into geological storage reservoirs such as depleted oil & gas reservoirs, saline aquifers and salt caverns regulated by the US EPA. It is a highly viscous liquid which is denser than the surrounding formation fluid, and so will sink in the reservoir and risk of buoyancy/upward migration is low. The bio-oil polymerizes (solidifies) on an expected timescale between 2–20 years, rendering it effectively immobile within the subsurface and therefore durable on geological timescales.

ISOprj_1J4P33N6W1S0RKE2.methodology: Subsurface Biomass Carbon Removal and Storage
ISOprj_1J4P33N6W1S0RKE2.description: Graphyte's Carbon Casting approach leverages waste biomass to permanently remove carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. Graphyte processes biomass into stable carbon blocks that are encased in an impermeable, long-lasting polymer material. These carbon blocks are then stored in a purpose-built storage site with a robust MRV system. Carbon Casting prevents the carbon blocks from decomposing over a 1000+ year timescale, which ensures that the carbon stored in the biomass will not be released back into the atmosphere in the form of CO2 or methane.

ISOprj_1J7NQMR9V1S04P0D.description: InPlanet works closely with farmers in the tropics to restore their soils and help them to transition to a low carbon, sustainable and nature-based agriculture. InPlanet do this through the deployment and scaling of Enhanced Weathering using locally sourced rocks that are optimal for CDR and regenerating nutrient-depleted soils.

ISOprj_1JCZCRW2S1S06KN0.description: Alt Carbon is a deeptech science and data company, building agri-infrastructure for Planetary Intelligence. They aim to make South Asia a hub for Carbon Dioxide Removal (CDR) through technology pathways like Enhanced Rock Weathering. They work with farmers and scientists in the Global South, to turn underutilized land into carbon sinks and aim to unite climate action with cultural and ecological restoration — by reviving degraded soils, restoring livelihoods, and rebuilding ecosystems. Alt Carbon are rooted in science, powered by community, and driven by the belief that revivals require ambitious people and audacious bets.

ISOprj_1JF8BBG921S010M4.description: Carboneers and Terrafront Ventures collaboratively develop biochar projects by processing agricultural residues into biochar and heat. In the project the biochar will be charged with both compost and manure, and given back for free to the same farmer. The aggregation of biomass and distribution of biochar is a 360 degree model. The project will be with rice, cotton and maize farmers in the regions of Odisha, Assam, Nagaland.

ISOprj_1JFA3YY9P1S0YVKR.description: CREW removes carbon dioxide from the atmosphere via wastewater treatment systems, deploying fine-grained natural minerals like calcium carbonate in wastewater treatment systems. Onsite, the feedstock is transferred into CREW's dosing systems, and is dosed into the wastewater treatment reactors as a slurry. CREW's system controls the rate of dosing to optimize process benefits and CDR.

ISOprj_1JKR5RQG81S0Y2CZ.description: Mati Carbon spreads rock dust onto agricultural fields in the Global South to support smallholder farmer resilience. The rock dust reacts with dissolved CO₂, converting it to bicarbonate, which durably removes CO₂ from the atmosphere. At the same time, the dissolution process releases micronutrients like Ca, Mg, Si, and Zn into the soil, improving crop health and productivity.

ISOprj_1JMAPP8SA1S0BQAJ.description: ZeroEx specializes in developing Enhanced Rock Weathering (ERW) projects in Germany, setting a focus on pioneering a novel, highly scalable MRV method that enhances measurement accuracy while reducing costs at scale. For our projects, we exclusively apply basaltic rock powders, derived as a by-product of existing mining operations. By testing over 100+ quarries, ZeroEx has secured supply of feedstocks with above-average CDR potentials and minimal heavy-metal concentrations, ensuring compliance with Germany's strict regulatory framework for water and soil protection and prioritizing environmental safety in all operations. By concentrating on local deployments with average transport distances under 30 km from the quarry to the field, ZeroEx minimizes its projects footprints and empowers local, family-owned farms to engage in sustainable initiatives, benefitting not only financially but also from several agronomic co-benefits such as the substitution of otherwise emissions-intensive agricultural liming.

ISOprj_1JN6XNWDQ1S0BSN7.description: Charm Industrial converts biomass residues (for example, corn stover, forestry residues) into bio-oil by heating the biomass quickly to very high temperatures. Charm uses woody or cellulosic residues in their pyrolysis and ensures that any emissions associated with growth or harvesting of this biomass are accounted for. This means waste biomass that would have otherwise decomposed is a preferred feedstock. The resulting bio-oil is low in energy content, but high in carbon content, and can be injected underground into geological storage reservoirs such as depleted oil & gas reservoirs, saline aquifers and salt caverns regulated by the US EPA. It is a highly viscous liquid which is denser than the surrounding formation fluid, and so will sink in the reservoir and risk of buoyancy/upward migration is low. The bio-oil polymerizes (solidifies) on an expected timescale between 2–20 years, rendering it effectively immobile within the subsurface and therefore durable on geological timescales.

ISOprj_1JPMVNV6K1S0WWRZ.description: agriCARBON produces biochar from biomass residues left over after biogas production in agricultural biogas plants. Agricultural businesses use biochar as a soil amendment for soil regeneration and transition to sustainable farming. Thanks to our solution, the circularity of efficient use of primary resources in the renewable energy production cycle is closed.

ISOprj_1JQ76PQZX1S04S93.description: Living Carbon revitalizes Appalachia by transforming severely degraded mine lands and marginal farmland into thriving, biodiverse forests. Combining cutting-edge science and innovative reforestation, Living Carbon turn scarred landscapes into high-value environmental assets — restoring ecosystems, and supporting local communities in a historically underserved region of the United States.

ISOprj_1JQ775W7D1S0WYSA.description: InPlanet works closely with farmers in the tropics to restore their soils and help them to transition to a low carbon, sustainable and nature-based agriculture. InPlanet do this through the deployment and scaling of Enhanced Weathering using locally sourced rocks that are optimal for CDR and regenerating nutrient-depleted soils.

ISOprj_1JQCK4WZX1S0ANXP.description: Clairity develops DAC technology which use low-cost and abundant alkali salts to remove CO₂ from the atmosphere. Atmospheric air is blown over a composite sorbent material that removes both CO₂ and H₂O, resulting in a process that is not only carbon negative but also water positive. Once saturated, the composite sorbent is heated to a low-temperature, regenerating the sorbent and releasing CO₂ and H₂O. The output CO₂ stream from Clairtiy's process can be sequestered or utilized across a range of pathways, enabling flexibility on storage to increase project deployments.

ISOprj_1JQEQKCF91S06HAJ.description: NULIFE GreenTech is a scalable, decentralized BiCRS solution that not only enables permanent carbon removal but also directly addresses real waste management challenges. By converting waste biomass—which would otherwise decompose and release emissions—into carbon-rich bio-oil, NULIFE provides a sustainable alternative to traditional disposal methods. NULIFE's modular HTL technology is highly flexible, processing a variety of engineered slurries containing both wet and dry organic wastes. The resulting bio-oil is transported for geological sequestration, ensuring permanent carbon removal. Additionally, NULIFE generates valuable co-products, including CO₂ gas and biochar, which can be leveraged for further carbon dioxide removal or to offset fossil fuels. The effluent water from the process can be recycled into the HTL system or repurposed to support regional water supply, enhancing sustainability.

ISOprj_1JQEW95GA1S0D2FD.description: Sitos Group is a BiCRS solution, converting biomass into high-quality biochar through advanced slow pyrolysis technology. This process thermally decomposes biomass in a low-oxygen environment, stabilizing carbon that would have otherwise returned to the atmosphere. The resulting biochar is used by farmers to enhance soil health, improve water retention, and boost crop yields—all while ensuring durable carbon removal. Made by growers, used by growers, Sitos Group closes the loop on agricultural waste, transforming it into a long-term climate and soil solution.

ISOprj_1JRZWM3BP1S071QG.description: Carba takes sustainably sourced waste biomass and efficiently converts it to a solid carbon charcoal devoid of food value. The solid carbon is then buried underground in anoxic chambers to protect it from oxidative and light-mediated degradation pathways. The process mimics the formation and storage of similar carbon structures in coal 300 million years ago, which have remained stable around the world.

ISOprj_1JTZ7NRK81S0GA0S.description: B10 is a BiCRS company making use of sawmil waste that would otherwise be burned on the pile or left to decompose and Turing this waste into high quality biochar for long term storage. The final biochar is used in a variety of applications like agriculture, anaerobic digesters, mine reclamation where it's ultimately ending up in soil.

ISOprj_1JVC6T3VR1S0AJ5P.description: INTERCARBO is a carbon removal process that utilizes wood residues from sawmill operations to produce biochar through a pyrolysis process. This approach reduces carbon emissions and contributes to climate change mitigation. The resulting biochar not only sequesters carbon for extended periods but also improves soil health when applied to degraded or abandoned forest roads. By efficiently managing sawmill waste and integrating biochar production into sustainable forestry practices, the project supports carbon capture, soil restoration, and community resilience. As a BiCRS solution, the INTERCARBO aligns with global efforts to reduce atmospheric CO₂ and contributes to achieving net-zero emissions.

ISOprj_1JWX91R5E1S00PN0.description: Ground Up is building industrial-scale biochar production hubs across India. By leveraging organised agricultural networks, like sugar cultivation, Ground Up creates scalable supply chains for biomass acquisition and biochar distribution, alongside streamlined MRV processes that ensure traceability and impact. The company uses indigenous pyrolysis technology—designed and manufactured in India—making this an India-first solution to carbon removal at scale. Ground Up works with hundreds of thousands of farmers and employs proprietary application protocols to maximise the agronomic benefits of its biochar-based products.

ISOprj_1JXCRW5ST1S0EEKH.description: Pacific Biochar is a pioneering company leading the charge in durable carbon removal through our innovative biochar production model. Committed to mitigating climate change while leaving a legacy of fertile soil, Pacific Biochar specializes in the production and distribution of high-quality biochar products designed to sequester carbon while enhancing agricultural and industrial productivity. Our unique model utilizes existing biomass power plant infrastructure to produce biochar, enabling rapid scaling potential with low capital investments. The partnerships we make with these bioenergy facilities result in cascading community benefits including wildfire risk reduction, rural job growth, and improved food security.

ISOprj_1JY1YXDBS1S01Y05.description: Lithos deploys ex-situ carbon dioxide mineralization through enhanced rock weathering (ERW) on managed agricultural lands with empirical mass-balance for cost-effective empirical attribution. Lithos curates a superfine waste basalt (no new crushing or mining) as a soil amendment, converting atmospheric CO2 to dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC), which is transported to the ocean and remains stable for >10,000 years.

ISOprj_1JYCV03BW1S0RTE5.description: Alt Carbon is a deeptech science and data company, building agri-infrastructure for Planetary Intelligence. They aim to make South Asia a hub for Carbon Dioxide Removal (CDR) through technology pathways like Enhanced Rock Weathering. They work with farmers and scientists in the Global South, to turn underutilized land into carbon sinks and aim to unite climate action with cultural and ecological restoration — by reviving degraded soils, restoring livelihoods, and rebuilding ecosystems. Alt Carbon are rooted in science, powered by community, and driven by the belief that revivals require ambitious people and audacious bets.

ISOprj_1JYDZZ4MS1S0MF77.description: Propagate is an agroforestry and reforestation developer that partners with farmers and landowners across the eastern United States to grow trees on agricultural land. Propagate's technical service staff has over 40 years of collective experience advising on agroforestry projects across over 30,000 acres across pre-planning, planning, design, site-leasing, site preparation, planting, and monitoring.

ISOprj_1JYENJXB71S0CR1B.description: CLG runs an industrial-scale biochar facility, using low-oxygen vacuum pyrolysis to turn biomass and to durable carbon and verifiable carbon credits. CLG sources feedstock through public-private partnerships with government departments, reducing landfill use and wildfire risk. Syngas byproduct powers the facility, turning waste into power.

ISOprj_1JYGSV7SE1S03PH9.description: Varhad specializes in converting agri waste (such as cotton stalk, pigeon pea etc) and biomass residue into valuable biochar using its own in-house pyrolisis reactors which are being built with robust technology. The biochar is blended with organic compost and added back to the soil for soil enrichment.

ISOprj_1JZ0ZD3JN1S0SHW9.description: Mombak is a multi-pathway carbon removal company operating large-scale Reforestation and Enhanced Rock Weathering (ERW) projects in Brazil. Our reforestation program transforms degraded pasturelands into biodiverse carbon sinks through native species planting and assisted natural regeneration. We actively neutralize leakage from our project areas and guarantee 100-year durability through continuous satellite monitoring of our forests. Our ERW projects spread finely ground rock on agricultural soils, where it captures atmospheric CO₂ as stable bicarbonates stored in the ocean on geological timescales — while improving soil health and crop yields for farmers. Across both pathways, we apply rigorous MRV protocols to deliver transparent, science-based carbon removal at scale.

ISOprj_1JZJY8NY61S0RH07.description: Alt Carbon is a deeptech science and data company, building agri-infrastructure for Planetary Intelligence. They aim to make South Asia a hub for Carbon Dioxide Removal (CDR) through technology pathways like Enhanced Rock Weathering. They work with farmers and scientists in the Global South, to turn underutilized land into carbon sinks and aim to unite climate action with cultural and ecological restoration — by reviving degraded soils, restoring livelihoods, and rebuilding ecosystems. Alt Carbon are rooted in science, powered by community, and driven by the belief that revivals require ambitious people and audacious bets.

ISOprj_1K051N4HQ1S02170.description: Corigin is a carbon removal business that uses a proprietary biorefinery technology to continuous convert biomass wastes into biochars that increase soil fertility and bio-oils for permanent deep geologic storage. We've been operating a pilot plant in California's Central Valley for over 4-years. Key technology advantages are 80% product yield on biomass (1,000 KG converts into 830 Kg of product), continuous production, scalable to multiple tons/hour throughput, and feedstock agnostic - can process virtually any plant or manure-based waste.

ISOprj_1K09XZV1B1S023XT.description: Through river alkalinity enhancement (RAE), site-specific amounts of safe alkalinity material is added to rivers where it dissolves rapidly, converting the CO2 in the rivers into stable, beneficial bicarbonate as well as minerals like calcium and magnesium. Our process absorbs CO₂ from both the soil and atmosphere and re-establishes key ecological building blocks. The rivers naturally transport the bicarbonate to the ocean, and the permanence of the CDR is currently estimated to be in the 10,000s of  years. The drawdown of carbon can be directly measured in the river in real time.

ISOprj_1K10D531D1S0DEV9.description: Terradot accelerates the natural process of rock weathering by applying finely ground silicate rock to tropical agricultural soils. Once applied, the rock dissolves in the presence of moisture and acidity, releasing base cations like calcium and magnesium that react with carbon dioxide in the soil to form bicarbonate, a stable form of carbon that is then safely transported through water systems to the ocean. This process ultimately shifts atmospheric CO₂ into the ocean's long-term carbon cycle, where it remains sequestered for hundreds of thousands of years.

ISOprj_1K1GX4BDK1S0FZVC.description: Gigafex captures carbon by converting agricultural waste, specifically pressed empty fruit bunches from palm oil production, into stable biochar using proprietary pyrolysis reactors located onsite. Their key partner, Coopeagropal, supplies a steady, traceable stream of this biomass, minimizing transport emissions. The biochar is then applied to nearby plantations to improve soil health and store carbon safely. The project aims to remove over 6,000 tonnes of CO₂ annually, with rigorous monitoring to ensure transparency and durability.

ISOprj_1K1T6SHXE1S0F3H4.description: Carbono Capital provides a Carbon Removal (BiCRS) solution that transforms waste biomass into biochar through biogenic-fueled pyrolysis. Using off-grid kilns, the process produces a soil-enhancing material that, when blended with compost and applied to agricultural land, improves soil fertility, protects crop biodiversity, and strengthens food security for rural communities.

ISOprj_1K21RKWYX1S0NWN6.siteLocation: The State of Mato Grosso do Sul
ISOprj_1K21RKWYX1S0NWN6.description: InPlanet works closely with farmers in the tropics to restore their soils and help them to transition to a low carbon, sustainable and nature-based agriculture. InPlanet do this through the deployment and scaling of Enhanced Weathering using locally sourced rocks that are optimal for CDR and regenerating nutrient-depleted soils.

ISOprj_1K2YPGE781S0A3Q0.description: Carboneers and Terrafront Ventures collaboratively develop biochar projects by processing agricultural residues into biochar and heat. In the project the biochar will be charged with both compost and manure, and given back for free to the same farmer. The aggregation of biomass and distribution of biochar is a 360 degree model. The project will be with rice, cotton and maize farmers in the regions of Odisha, Assam, Nagaland.

ISOprj_1K39D0N8S1S0TMKX.description: Through river alkalinity enhancement (RAE), site-specific amounts of safe alkalinity material is added to rivers where it dissolves rapidly, converting the CO2 in the rivers into stable, beneficial bicarbonate as well as minerals like calcium and magnesium. Our process absorbs CO₂ from both the soil and atmosphere and re-establishes key ecological building blocks. The rivers naturally transport the bicarbonate to the ocean, and the permanence of the CDR is currently estimated to be in the 10,000s of  years. The drawdown of carbon can be directly measured in the river in real time.

ISOprj_1K3MGXD4A1S0S3H8.description: Silica removes atmospheric CO₂ by accelerating the Earth's natural rock weathering cycle. We partner with farmers in Latin America to apply highly reactive volcanic rockdust to agricultural fields, permanently removing CO₂ while improving crop yields and building climate resilience. We are first focusing on tropical regions of Mexico, where conditions are naturally favorable for faster CO₂ removal and outsized agronomic benefits.

ISOprj_1K3S0527T1S0KYXT.description: CREW removes carbon dioxide from the atmosphere via wastewater treatment systems, deploying fine-grained natural minerals like calcium carbonate in wastewater treatment systems. Onsite, the feedstock is transferred into CREW's dosing systems, and is dosed into the wastewater treatment reactors as a slurry. CREW's system controls the rate of dosing to optimize process benefits and CDR.

ISOprj_1K3VWSDS61S0QKV7.description: Equilibrium's BiCRS project converts invasive woody biomass, into durable biochar for long-term carbon sequestration. Using advanced pyrolysis technology, the project addresses critical environmental challenges, including land degradation and biodiversity loss. By diverting biomass from combustion and decay into a stable carbon form, the initiative delivers measurable climate benefits, enhances soil health, and supports sustainable rural livelihoods in one of India's most water-stressed regions.

ISOprj_1K48633C61S0WY58.description: CarbonZero.ECO operates Beston BST-50S pyrolysis systems that use a continuous rotary kiln design with an enclosed burn chamber. Biomass, such as almond shells, is heated in a low-oxygen environment, preventing combustion and converting the material into stable biochar. The process captures and reuses syngas for heat, improving efficiency and reducing emissions. This closed-loop system ensures consistent, high-quality biochar production while maximizing carbon retention and minimizing environmental impact.

ISOprj_1K4PWG5T01S0PWMF.description:
The Bharat Biochar Initiative is a BiCRS (Biochar Carbon Removal & Sequestration) solution. It takes naturally fallen pine needles from Uttarakhand, which would have otherwise contributed to forest fires, and repurposes them to create biochar. This process uses a continuous reactor technology to produce a carbon-rich substance for agricultural and environmental use.

By doing so, the project mitigates wildfire risks, promotes carbon sequestration, and generates rural livelihoods.

ISOprj_1K4SN1CT61S0NZ7N.description: Planeteers captures CO₂ in water and unleashes the potential of the oceans as the largest carbon sink on our planet. The lab-proven, fully-measurable, scalable, and multi-CO₂-source technology to capture and store CO₂ leverages the natural process of limestone weathering and accelerates it from thousands of years in nature to a few minutes with our reactor technology. The result of this chemical reaction is hydrogen carbonate which is stored in the ocean for a very long period (10,000+ years) and has a positive "healing"-effect to work against ocean acidification.

ISOprj_1K4XA2FF31S0T7V9.description: The projects utilize a 4 ton-per-hour per biomass carbonization Production line, initially processing 16,000 metric tons of agricultural waste annually to produce biochar. Pyrolysis occurs at temperatures exceeding 600°C, ensuring efficient carbonization while minimizing emissions. The resulting biochar, with an estimated carbon content of 74% and an H:C ratio of 0.38, is applied as a soil amendment to enhance agricultural productivity and sequester carbon for over 1,000 years. The project also captures and reuses pyrolysis gases for energy efficiency.

ISOprj_1K56VP7FE1S0QDSH.description: The project generates solutions to the diseased arecanut trees in the Garo Hills region of Meghalaya, northeastern part of India. Areca nut cultivation forms the bedrock of the local economy, but the airborne disease has devasted impacts plantation and on the farmers' livelihood. The project converts dead areca nut trees into biochar through controlled pyrolysis at ~450–550°C under limited oxygen conditions. This process stabilizes biogenic carbon, preventing methane emissions from natural decay while producing a carbon-rich soil amendment that enhances soil structure and nutrient retention. While the disease is preventable, once the plants succumb, there is no alternative. Currently, the farmers are not able to utilize the dead stems that are lying and degrading naturally, leading to termite infestation. The farmers are also not using the land where the dead stems are standing. This presents an opportunity for Biochar production and exploring local application using soil mineralization.

ISOprj_1K6G4S1PJ1S0TR4Z.description: Dark Earth Carbon is an East Africa–based carbon removal company deploying high-temperature pyrolysis systems to transform low-value biomass residues into durable biochar. Their continuous rotary kilns are engineered for tropical conditions, achieving high throughput and stable carbon yields with minimal energy loss. Each facility integrates advanced digital MRV for real-time carbon accounting and traceable registry issuance, ensuring transparent, verifiable removals. Dark Earth Carbon's technology delivers reliable, low-cost carbon sequestration with strong agronomic and environmental co-benefits, enhancing soils, supporting regenerative agriculture, and advancing climate resilience in emerging markets.

ISOprj_1K7F70BKD1S04GWB.description: The Morobe Markham Reforestation project is a first-of-its-kind reforestation project in the Markham Valley of Morobe Province, Papua New Guinea. It is a partnership between Morobe Markham LLC, the developing partner with extensive experience managing emission reduction projects in Papua New Guinea, PNG Carbon Estate, a team of expert local foresters and plantation experts, and Nature Focus Capital, an experienced fund-raiser and manager of carbon emission reduction projects. The project has hired Global Carbon Resources, a US-based carbon project management company, to manage the project, develop the processes and documentation to get the credits issued, sell the carbon credits and distribute the profits according to the agreements with the ILGs within the context of the government regulations.  The project aims to take lands that were once forests and are now degraded grasslands and restore them with native species through an initial shelter wood planting with understory enrichment after three years of growth.

ISOprj_1K7HK8Q4S1S0D4W4.description: Vaulted is a BiCRS solution, taking end-of-life organic waste that otherwise would have decomposed, and geologically sequestering the waste for storage. Vaulted secures a range of end-of-life organic wastes (including biosolids, livestock and agricultural waste, paper sludge, and others) through sustainable sourcing practices, and deploys slurry injection technology to geologically sequester these wastes for the purpose of permanent carbon removal.

ISOprj_1K8BE4BSR1S06DWN.siteLocation: Rio Verde, state of Goiás, Brazil
ISOprj_1K8BE4BSR1S06DWN.description: Anglo American's Earthstone project uses a magnesium silicate by-product from ferronickel production in an enhanced rock weathering application. In magnesium depleted soils surrounding the ferronickel operations in Brazil, this provides not only controlled released magnesium but also a liming effect which is beneficial for crop health and can show significant yield increases for farmers.

ISOprj_1K9A90ZPH1S0ZJ9S.description: Carbon Ventures Africa is a nature-based carbon removal company working with local communities to restore degraded forest landscapes. Through native tree planting, assisted natural regeneration, and long-term forest protection, CVA converts degraded forest land into stable, biodiverse forests. These restored ecosystems capture and store atmospheric CO₂ in living biomass and soils for verified, durable carbon removal, monitored through field measurement and remote-sensing technologies.

ISOprj_1K9W3ZCY71S0NRMS.description:
Nordic Carbon was founded on a mission to turn waste into value, both for the local communities and the global environment. They source biomass residues and establish strong local partnerships to ensure long-term viability. They tailor-make, efficient biochar systems to meet the technical cultural and environmental context locally; and build, install and operate complete carbon removal facilities optimized for performance, durability and transparency.

With 20+ years of experience in the biomass industry from top management and operations, the team behind Nordic Carbon brings extensive expertise in sourcing, production, logistics, sustainability and commercialisation.

ISOprj_1KA8WSNN61S09FHS.description: Kisiwa Farming and atmosfair run a pyrolysis plant on Mafia Island in Tanzania, producing biochar from surplus coconut biomass. Instead of burning non-recyclable pruning residues from coconut palm trees and other biomass residues from the restoration of coconut plantations in the field, they are used to produce biochar. The biochar is used to store carbon, improve soil quality and increase crop yields, as well as replacing conventional fertilisers on the organic farm. The project aims to create a sustainable circular economy on the island that benefits all stakeholders.

ISOprj_1KA95092G1S093EM.description: Mombak is a multi-pathway carbon removal company operating large-scale Reforestation and Enhanced Rock Weathering (ERW) projects in Brazil. Our reforestation program transforms degraded pasturelands into biodiverse carbon sinks through native species planting and assisted natural regeneration. We actively neutralize leakage from our project areas and guarantee 100-year durability through continuous satellite monitoring of our forests. Our ERW projects spread finely ground rock on agricultural soils, where it captures atmospheric CO₂ as stable bicarbonates stored in the ocean on geological timescales — while improving soil health and crop yields for farmers. Across both pathways, we apply rigorous MRV protocols to deliver transparent, science-based carbon removal at scale.

ISOprj_1KBECJX991S0EDE4.description: Enable Earth processes agricultural waste in Thailand, otherwise landfilled or burnt, into biochar, capturing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and lowering air pollution. We also upgrade the waste heat from our process to green and continuous industrial heat for industrial boilers and generate electricity. Our modular solution can co-locate with existing factories to provide heat and electricity.

ISOprj_1KC8T0EGS1S0H36R.description: Earthrevive is a CDR developer working with farmers across engineered removal pathways.

ISOprj_1KCEM5PTM1S0MK7X.description: Alcom is a biochar project developer that is speeds the transition to a low-carbon world by transforming biomass and agricultural waste into clean fuels, clean energy, biochar, and high-quality carbon credits. Our technology creates super circular solutions by converting durable biochar into biofertilizer, bio-oil into biofuel and syngas into electricity. By optimizing co-products from our pyrolysis technology we ensure that we create maximum impact from our low-carbon solutions.

ISOprj_1KCNW12WM1S0AY3D.description: Our projects use a high-efficiency pyrolysis processes to heat leftover biomass—an agricultural residue that is normally burned or left to decompose. This process converts the biomass into biochar, a stable, solid form of charcoal that resists decomposition and functions as long-term carbon storage. The resulting biochar is then composted into a "Biofertilizer" and applied back to the soil, which helps improve soil health.

ISOprj_1KESD32TS1S0ZHGV.description: Biochar Solutions manufactures and sell biochar for remediation, agricultural, and industrial applications. Biomass is sourced through high hazard biomass reduction projects, wood recycling programs, and other non merchantable woody biomass residuals streams. Biochar Solutions is also creating biochar based products for a number of different applications and industries that allows its customers to integrate biochar into their existing programs or processes without changes to equipment or procedure.

ISOprj_1KFDNVSDZ1S0QA39.methodology: Subsurface Biomass Carbon Removal and Storage
ISOprj_1KFDNVSDZ1S0QA39.description: Rewind cleans CO₂ from the atmosphere by relocating residual plants to the deep Black Sea. This is a nature-based approach, as all rivers wash organic carbon out to sea, and the Black Sea is the world's largest anoxic basin, naturally preserving carbon for thousands of years. Rewind is developing the science, certification, licensing policy, and MRV technology, to allow existing supply chains to transport and lock away gigaton-scale carbon within this decade.

ISOprj_1KFTFVQTY1S08RE0.description: Carboneyes partners with sugarcane mills to carbonise waste bagasse that would otherwise be dumped in large open heaps, where it releases CO2, methane and acidic leachate as it decomposes. The bagasse is converted into biochar through pyrolysis, preventing these emissions and locking the carbon into a stable form that remains in the soil for centuries. Carboneyes works directly with smallholder sugarcane farmers to apply the biochar to degraded soils, increasing soil organic carbon and restoring soil health. This boosts yields, reduces fertiliser dependence and creates a durable carbon sink that supports climate resilience and farmer livelihoods.

ISOprj_1KHT9B45F1S0HY3H.description: Our projects use a high-efficiency pyrolysis processes to heat leftover biomass—an agricultural residue that is normally burned or left to decompose. This process converts the biomass into biochar, a stable, solid form of charcoal that resists decomposition and functions as long-term carbon storage. The resulting biochar is then composted into a "Biofertilizer" and applied back to the soil, which helps improve soil health.

ISOprj_1KJQ2NM0R1S09256.description: Bigadan employs advanced anaerobic digestion technology to convert organic waste—material that would otherwise decompose and emit methane and CO₂—into renewable bioenergy. The company processes a diverse range of substrates, including insulin residues, enzyme byproducts, and agricultural manure. By integrating carbon capture and storage (CCS) solutions into its operations, Bigadan ensures the permanent and secure removal of biogenic carbon.

ISOprj_1KNSEH7NT1S052MH.description: re.green restores native forests for people and the planet, leveraging advanced technology and exceptional operational capacity to restore ecosystems at scale in the Atlantic Forest and Amazon. With precision, re.green identifies degraded areas, selects ideal native species, deploys scientists on the ground, and engages local communities, fostering training and socio-economic development. From seed collection to the commercialization of nature-based solutions, re.green delivers transformative results. Its projects generate carbon credits using the most advanced ecological restoration methods, setting a new standard of excellence in the sector.

ISOprj_1KQSRWYTB1S0R69E.description: Equilibrium's BiCRS project converts invasive woody biomass, into durable biochar for long-term carbon sequestration. Using advanced pyrolysis technology, the project addresses critical environmental challenges, including land degradation and biodiversity loss. By diverting biomass from combustion and decay into a stable carbon form, the initiative delivers measurable climate benefits, enhances soil health, and supports sustainable rural livelihoods in one of India's most water-stressed regions.
